above.pali: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici bhayāni uppajjanti sabbāni tāni bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
above.sujato: In the same way, whatever dangers there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.
above.english: so too, whatever perils arise … all arise on account of the fool, not on account of the wise person.

lines.pali: Ye keci upaddavā uppajjanti sabbe te bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.

lines.pali: Ye keci upasaggā uppajjanti sabbe te bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.

below.pali: Iti kho, bhikkhave, sappaṭibhayo bālo, appaṭibhayo paṇḍito.
below.sujato: So, the fool is dangerous, but the astute person is safe.
below.english: (1) Thus, bhikkhus, the fool brings peril, the wise person brings no peril;

above.sujato: In the same way, an individual often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.
above.english: so too, some person often goes to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma from the bhikkhus….

lines.pali: Tassa bhikkhū dhammaṁ desenti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsenti.
lines.sujato: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

lines.pali: So tasmiṁ āsane nisinno tassā kathāya neva ādiṁ manasi karoti, na majjhaṁ manasi karoti, na pariyosānaṁ manasi karoti;
lines.sujato: But even while sitting there, that person doesn’t apply the mind to the discussion in the beginning, middle, or end.

below.pali: vuṭṭhitopi tamhā āsanā tassā kathāya neva ādiṁ manasi karoti, na majjhaṁ manasi karoti, na pariyosānaṁ manasi karoti.
below.sujato: And when they rise from their seat, they don’t apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.
below.english: After he has risen from his seat, he still does not attend to that talk at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.

above.pali: Rāge pahīne nevattabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
above.sujato: When greed has been given up, they don’t intend to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They don’t experience mental pain and sadness.
above.english: But when lust is abandoned, he does not intend for his own affliction, for the affliction of others, or for the affliction of both, and he does not experience mental suffering and dejection.

lines.pali: Ratto kho …pe… kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
Rāge pahīne neva kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, na vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, na manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
Ratto kho …pe… attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
Rāge pahīne attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.

below.pali: Evampi kho, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti …pe….
below.sujato: This is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.
below.english: It is in this way that the Dhamma is directly visible….

above.pali: mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, nāññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalan’ti.
above.sujato: Only what is given to my disciples is very fruitful, not what is given to the disciples of others.’
above.english: only what is given to my disciples is very fruitful, not what is given to the disciples of others.”’

lines.pali: Ye te, bho gotama, evamāhaṁsu ‘samaṇo gotamo evamāha:
Mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dānaṁ dātabbaṁ, nāññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dānaṁ dātabbaṁ.
Mayhameva dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, nāññesaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ.
Mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, nāññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalan”’ti.

below.pali: Kacci te bhoto gotamassa vuttavādino na ca bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānupāto gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati?
below.sujato: I trust those who say this repeat what the worthy Gotama has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?
below.english: Do those who speak thus state what has been said by Master Gotama and not misrepresent him with what is contrary to fact? Do they explain in accordance with the Dhamma so that they would not incur any reasonable criticism or ground for censure?

above.pali: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama.
above.sujato: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!
above.english: “Excellent, Master Gotama! …

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
lines.sujato: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

lines.pali: Esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi, dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
lines.sujato: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

below.pali: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
below.sujato: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
below.english: Let Master Gotama consider me a lay follower who from today has gone for refuge for life.”

above.pali: Assosuṁ kho te bhikkhū sarabhassa paribbājakassa rājagahe parisati evaṁ vācaṁ bhāsamānassa:
above.sujato: They heard what Sarabha was saying.
above.english: They then heard the wanderer Sarabha making such a statement to an assembly in Rājagaha.

lines.pali: Aññāya ca panāhaṁ samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtikānaṁ dhammaṁ evāhaṁ tasmā dhammavinayā apakkanto”ti.

mind with hate as “mind with hate”,
and mind without hate as “mind without hate”;
mind with delusion as “mind with delusion”,
and mind without delusion as “mind without delusion”;
mind that is not supreme as “mind that is not supreme”,
and mind that is supreme as “mind that is supreme”;
mind immersed in samādhi as “mind immersed in samādhi”,
and mind not immersed in samādhi as “mind not immersed in samādhi”;

above.sujato: A noble disciple who wants to be beautiful ought not pray for it, or hope for it, or pine for it.
above.english: (2) “Householder, the noble disciple who desires beauty …

above.pali: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported what had happened.

lines.pali: “idha, bhante, sāvatthiyaṁ ubho mātāputtā vassāvāsaṁ upagamiṁsu—
bhikkhu ca bhikkhunī ca, te aññamaññassa abhiṇhaṁ dassanakāmā ahesuṁ, mātāpi puttassa abhiṇhaṁ dassanakāmā ahosi, puttopi mātaraṁ abhiṇhaṁ dassanakāmo ahosi.
Tesaṁ abhiṇhaṁ dassanā saṁsaggo ahosi, saṁsagge sati vissāso ahosi, vissāse sati otāro ahosi, te otiṇṇacittā sikkhaṁ apaccakkhāya dubbalyaṁ anāvikatvā methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭiseviṁsū”ti.

below.pali: “Kiṁ nu so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso maññati:
below.sujato: “Mendicants, how could that futile man imagine that
below.english: The Blessed One said: “Bhikkhus, did that foolish man think:

above.pali: Atha kho so bhikkhu taṁ saddhivihārikaṁ bhikkhuṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then that mendicant took his protégé to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
above.english: Then the preceptor took his pupil to the Blessed One. He paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side, and told the Blessed One what his pupil had said.

lines.pali: ‘etarahi me, bhante, madhurakajāto ceva kāyo, disā ca maṁ na pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca me nappaṭibhanti, thinamiddhañca me cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, atthi ca me dhammesu vicikicchā’”ti.
lines.sujato: ‘Now, sir, my body feels like it’s drugged. I’m disorientated, the teachings don’t spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness fill my mind. I lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, and have doubts about the teachings.’”

below.pali: “Evañhetaṁ, bhikkhu, hoti indriyesu aguttadvārassa, bhojane amattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttassa, avipassakassa kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ, pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogaṁ ananuyuttassa viharato, yaṁ madhurakajāto ceva kāyo hoti, disā cassa na pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca taṁ nappaṭibhanti, thinamiddhañcassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carati, hoti cassa dhammesu vicikicchā.
below.sujato: “That’s how it is, mendicant, when your sense doors are unguarded, you eat too much, you’re not dedicated to wakefulness, you’re unable to discern skillful qualities, and you don’t pursue the development of the qualities on the side of awakening in the evening and toward dawn. Your body feels like it’s drugged. You’re disorientated, the teachings don’t spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness fill your mind. You lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, and have doubts about the teachings.
below.english: The Blessed One said: “So it is, bhikkhu! (1) When one is unguarded in the doors of the sense faculties, (2) immoderate in eating, (3) and not intent on wakefulness; (4) when one lacks insight into wholesome qualities (5) and does not dwell intent on the endeavor to develop the aids to enlightenment in the earlier and later phases of the night, one’s body seems as if it had been drugged, one becomes disoriented, and the teachings are no longer clear to one. Dullness and drowsiness obsess one’s mind. One lives the spiritual life dissatisfied and has doubt about the teachings.

above.pali: Atha kho so bhikkhu taṁ saddhivihārikaṁ bhikkhuṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then that mendicant took his protégé to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
above.english: Then the preceptor took his pupil to the Blessed One. He paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side, and told the Blessed One what his pupil had said.

lines.pali: ‘etarahi me, bhante, na ceva madhurakajāto kāyo, disā ca me pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca maṁ paṭibhanti, thinamiddhañca me cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, abhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, natthi ca me dhammesu vicikicchā’”ti.
lines.sujato: ‘Now, sir, my body doesn’t feel like it’s drugged. I’m not disorientated, the teachings spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness don’t fill my mind. I lead the spiritual life satisfied, and have no doubts about the teachings.’”

below.pali: “Evañhetaṁ, bhikkhu, hoti indriyesu guttadvārassa, bhojane mattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ anuyuttassa, vipassakassa kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ, pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogaṁ anuyuttassa viharato, yaṁ na ceva madhurakajāto kāyo hoti, disā cassa pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca taṁ paṭibhanti, thinamiddhañcassa cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, abhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carati, na cassa hoti dhammesu vicikicchā.
below.sujato: “That’s how it is, mendicant, when your sense doors are guarded, you’re moderate in eating, you’re dedicated to wakefulness, you’re able to discern skillful qualities, and you pursue the development of the qualities on the side of awakening in the evening and toward dawn. Your body doesn’t feel like it’s drugged. You’re not disorientated, the teachings spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness don’t fill your mind. You lead the spiritual life satisfied, and have no doubts about the teachings.
below.english: The Blessed One said: “So it is, bhikkhu! When one is guarded in the doors of the sense faculties, moderate in eating, and intent on wakefulness; when one has insight into wholesome qualities and dwells intent on the endeavor to develop the aids to enlightenment in the earlier and later phases of the night, one’s body does not seem as if it had been drugged, one becomes well oriented, and the teachings are clear to one. Dullness and drowsiness do not obsess one’s mind. One lives the spiritual life joyfully and has no doubt about the teachings.

above.pali: Idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, atthavasaṁ paṭicca ‘kammassakomhi, kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo, yaṁ kammaṁ karissāmi—
above.sujato: This is the advantage for a woman or a man, a layperson or a renunciate of often reviewing like this: ‘I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds. Deeds are my womb, my relative, and my refuge.
above.english: It is for the sake of this benefit that a woman or a man, a householder or one gone forth, should often reflect thus: ‘I am the owner of my kamma, the heir of my kamma; I have kamma as my origin, kamma as my relative, kamma as my resort; I will be the heir of whatever kamma, good or bad, that I do.’

lines.sujato: I shall be the heir of whatever deeds I do, whether good or bad.’

lines.pali: Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā manāpakāyikā devatā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhante, tā devatā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
‘mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, manāpakāyikā nāma devatā tīsu ṭhānesu issariyaṁ kārema vasaṁ vattema.
Mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, yādisakaṁ vaṇṇaṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ vaṇṇaṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma;
yādisakaṁ saraṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ saraṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma;
yādisakaṁ sukhaṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ sukhaṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma.
Mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, manāpakāyikā nāma devatā imesu tīsu ṭhānesu issariyaṁ kārema vasaṁ vattemā’ti.
‘aho vatimā devatā sabbāva nīlā assu nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā’ti.
Atha kho, bhante, tā devatā mama cittamaññāya sabbāva nīlā ahesuṁ nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā.

lines.sujato: “Reverends, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for having no regrets.
When there are regrets, one who has regrets has destroyed a vital condition for joy. …
One who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rukkho sākhāpalāsavipanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi … pheggupi … sāropi na pāripūriṁ gacchati.
lines.sujato: Suppose there was a tree that lacked branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would not grow to fullness.

lines.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro;
lines.sujato: In the same way, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for having no regrets.
When there are regrets, one who has regrets has destroyed a vital condition for joy. …
One who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

lines.sujato: Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

lines.pali: ‘ime diṭṭhiṭṭhānā evaṅgahitā evaṁparāmaṭṭhā evaṅgatikā bhavanti evaṁabhisamparāyā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘If you hold on to and attach to these grounds for views it leads to such a destiny in the next life.’

lines.pali: Tañca tathāgato pajānāti, tato ca uttaritaraṁ pajānāti, tañca pajānanaṁ na parāmasati, aparāmasato cassa paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā.
lines.sujato: He understands this, and what goes beyond this. And since he does not misapprehend that understanding, he has realized quenching within himself.

lines.pali: Vedanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā anupādāvimutto, bhikkhave, tathāgato.
lines.sujato: Having truly understood the origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape from feelings, the Realized One is freed by not grasping.

below.pali: Ime kho te, bhikkhave, dhammā gambhīrā duddasā duranubodhā santā paṇītā atakkāvacarā nipuṇā paṇḍitavedanīyā, ye tathāgato sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti, yehi tathāgatassa yathābhuccaṁ vaṇṇaṁ sammā vadamānā vadeyyuṁ.
below.sujato: These are the principles—deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, comprehensible to the astute—which the Realized One makes known after realizing them with his own insight. And those who genuinely praise the Realized One would rightly speak of these things.
below.english: and it is concerning these that those who would praise the Tathāgata in accordance with reality would speak.

above.pali: “ayaṁ, deva, makkhali gosālo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto.
above.sujato: “Your Majesty, this bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people. He is of long standing, long gone forth; he is advanced in years and has reached the final stage of life.

lines.sujato: Let Your Majesty pay homage to him.

lines.pali: Appeva nāma devassa makkhaliṁ gosālaṁ payirupāsato cittaṁ pasīdeyyā”ti.
lines.sujato: Hopefully in so doing your mind will find peace.”

above.sujato: The substances of earth, water, fire, air; pleasure, pain, and the soul is the seventh.
above.english: The body of earth, the body of water, the body of fire, the body of air, pleasure, pain, and the soul as the seventh.

lines.pali: ime satta kāyā akaṭā akaṭavidhā animmitā animmātā vañjhā kūṭaṭṭhā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā.
lines.sujato: These seven substances are not made, not derived, not created, without a creator, barren, steady as a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar.

lines.pali: Te na iñjanti, na vipariṇamanti, na aññamaññaṁ byābādhenti, nālaṁ aññamaññassa sukhāya vā dukkhāya vā sukhadukkhāya vā.
lines.sujato: They don’t move or deteriorate or obstruct each other. They’re unable to cause pleasure, pain, or both pleasure and pain to each other.

below.pali: Tattha natthi hantā vā ghātetā vā, sotā vā sāvetā vā, viññātā vā viññāpetā vā.
below.sujato: And here there is no one who kills or who makes others kill; no one who learns or who educates others; no one who understands or who helps others understand.
below.english: Among these there is no killer nor one who causes killing; no hearer nor one who causes hearing; no cognizer nor one who causes cognition.

lines.sujato: ‘This is the most foolish and stupid of all these ascetics and brahmins!

so, deva, kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito.
So evaṁ pabbajito samāno kāyena saṁvuto viharati, vācāya saṁvuto viharati, manasā saṁvuto viharati, ghāsacchādanaparamatāya santuṭṭho, abhirato paviveke’ti.

lines.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho pubbe iṇaṁ ādāya kammante payojesiṁ.
Sohaṁ yāni ca porāṇāni iṇamūlāni, tāni ca byantiṁ akāsiṁ, atthi ca me uttariṁ avasiṭṭhaṁ dārabharaṇāyā’ti.

below.pali: So tatonidānaṁ labhetha pāmojjaṁ, adhigaccheyya somanassaṁ.
below.sujato: he’d be filled with joy and happiness.
below.english: and as a result he would become glad and experience joy.

above.pali: Tassa evamassa:
above.sujato: Thinking about this,
above.english: He would reflect on this,

lines.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho pubbe ābādhiko ahosiṁ dukkhito bāḷhagilāno;
bhattañca me nacchādesi, na ca me āsi kāye balamattā.
bhattañca me chādeti, atthi ca me kāye balamattā’ti.

below.pali: So tatonidānaṁ labhetha pāmojjaṁ, adhigaccheyya somanassaṁ.
below.sujato: they’d be filled with joy and happiness.
below.english: and as a result he would become glad and experience joy.

above.pali: Tassa evamassa:
above.sujato: Thinking about this,
above.english: He would reflect on this,

lines.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho pubbe bandhanāgāre baddho ahosiṁ, somhi etarahi tamhā bandhanāgārā mutto sotthinā abbhayena.
Natthi ca me kiñci bhogānaṁ vayo’ti.

below.pali: So tatonidānaṁ labhetha pāmojjaṁ, adhigaccheyya somanassaṁ.
below.sujato: they’d be filled with joy and happiness.
below.english: and as a result he would become glad and experience joy.

above.pali: Tassa evamassa:
above.sujato: Thinking about this,
above.english: He would reflect on this,

lines.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho pubbe dāso ahosiṁ anattādhīno parādhīno na yenakāmaṅgamo.
Somhi etarahi tamhā dāsabyā mutto attādhīno aparādhīno bhujisso yenakāmaṅgamo’ti.

below.pali: So tatonidānaṁ labhetha pāmojjaṁ, adhigaccheyya somanassaṁ.
below.sujato: they’d be filled with joy and happiness.
below.english: and as a result he would become glad and experience joy.

above.sujato: Thinking about this,
above.english: He would reflect on this,

lines.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho pubbe sadhano sabhogo kantāraddhānamaggaṁ paṭipajjiṁ dubbhikkhaṁ sappaṭibhayaṁ.
Somhi etarahi taṁ kantāraṁ nitthiṇṇo sotthinā, gāmantaṁ anuppatto khemaṁ appaṭibhayan’ti.

below.pali: So tatonidānaṁ labhetha pāmojjaṁ, adhigaccheyya somanassaṁ.
below.sujato: they’d be filled with joy and happiness.
below.english: and as a result he would become glad and experience joy.

above.pali: So parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti—
above.sujato: They understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.
above.english: He understands the minds of other beings and persons, having encompassed them with his own mind.

below.pali: Idampi kho, mahārāja, sandiṭṭhikaṁ sāmaññaphalaṁ purimehi sandiṭṭhikehi sāmaññaphalehi abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.
below.sujato: This too, Great King, is a fruit of the ascetic life that’s apparent in the present life which is better and finer than the former ones.
below.english: This too, great king, is a visible fruit of recluseship more excellent and sublime than the previous ones.

above.pali: ‘So idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
above.english: He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’ …

lines.pali: ‘Ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
Tassa evaṁ jānato evaṁ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati,

below.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
below.english: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further beyond this.’

above.pali: “tatrānanda, yamidaṁ asaññasattāyatanaṁ.
above.english: “If one understands the remaining stations for consciousness … the base of non-percipient beings … the base of neither perception nor non-perception, and if one understands its origin, its passing away, its satisfaction, its unsatisfactoriness, and the escape from it, is it proper for one to seek enjoyment in it?”

lines.pali: Yo nu kho, ānanda, tañca pajānāti, tassa ca samudayaṁ pajānāti, tassa ca atthaṅgamaṁ pajānāti, tassa ca assādaṁ pajānāti, tassa ca ādīnavaṁ pajānāti, tassa ca nissaraṇaṁ pajānāti, kallaṁ nu tena tadabhinanditun”ti?

below.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
below.english: “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

above.pali: Yassa, bhikkhave, dhamme manasikaroto anuppanno vā kāmāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā kāmāsavo pavaḍḍhati;
above.sujato: They are the things that, when the mind is applied to them, give rise to unarisen defilements and make arisen defilements grow: the defilements of sensual desire,
above.english: They are things such that when he attends to them, the unarisen taint of sensual desire arises in him…as §6…and the arisen taint of ignorance increases.

lines.pali: anuppanno vā bhavāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā bhavāsavo pavaḍḍhati;
anuppanno vā avijjāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā avijjāsavo pavaḍḍhati—

below.pali: ime dhammā na manasikaraṇīyā, ye dhamme na manasi karoti.
below.sujato: These are the things to which they don’t apply the mind and should not.
below.english: These are the things unfit for attention that he does not attend to.

above.pali: Yassa, bhikkhave, dhamme manasikaroto anuppanno vā kāmāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā kāmāsavo pahīyati;
above.sujato: They are the things that, when the mind is applied to them, do not give rise to unarisen defilements and give up arisen defilements: the defilements of sensual desire,
above.english: They are things such that when he attends to them, the unarisen taint of sensual desire does not arise in him…as §6…and the arisen taint of ignorance is abandoned.

lines.pali: anuppanno vā bhavāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā bhavāsavo pahīyati;

below.english: These are the things fit for attention that he attends to.

above.pali: anabhijjhālūhamasmi.
above.sujato: I am not full of desire …’
above.english: I am uncovetous…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā anabhijjhālū araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, anabhijjhālutaṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.pali: ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā byāpannacittā paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, byāpannacittapaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṁ bhayabheravaṁ avhāyanti.
below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins full of ill will, with malicious intentions …
below.english: “‘…with a mind of ill will and intentions of hate…

above.pali: mettacittohamasmi.
above.sujato: I have a heart full of love …’
above.english: I have a mind of loving-kindness…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā mettacittā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, mettacittataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.pali: ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhānasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṁ bhayabheravaṁ avhāyanti.
below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins overcome with dullness and drowsiness …
below.english: “‘…overcome by sloth and torpor…

above.pali: vigatathinamiddhohamasmi.
above.sujato: I am rid of dullness and drowsiness …’
above.english: I am without sloth and torpor…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā vigatathinamiddhā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vigatathinamiddhataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who are restless, with minds unsettled …
below.english: “‘…overcome with restlessness and unpeaceful in mind…

above.pali: vūpasantacittohamasmi.
above.sujato: My mind is settled …’
above.english: I have a peaceful mind…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā vūpasantacittā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vūpasantacittataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who are doubting and uncertain …
below.english: “‘…uncertain and doubting…

above.pali: tiṇṇavicikicchohamasmi.
above.sujato: I’ve gone beyond doubt …’
above.english: I have gone beyond doubt…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā tiṇṇavicikicchā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, tiṇṇavicikicchataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who glorify themselves and put others down …
below.english: “‘ …given to self-praise and disparagement of others…

above.pali: anattukkaṁsako aparavambhīhamasmi.
above.sujato: I don’t glorify myself and put others down …’
above.english: I am not given to self-praise and disparagement of others…’

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who are cowardly and craven …
below.english: “‘…subject to alarm and terror…

above.pali: vigatalomahaṁsohamasmi.
above.sujato: I don’t get startled …’
above.english: I am free from trepidation…’

Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vigatalomahaṁsataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who enjoy possessions, honor, and popularity …
below.english: “‘…desirous of gain, honour, and renown…

above.pali: appicchohamasmi.
above.sujato: I have few wishes …’
above.english: I have few wishes…’

Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, appicchataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who are lazy and lack energy …
below.english: “‘…lazy and wanting in energy…

above.pali: āraddhavīriyohamasmi.
above.sujato: I am energetic …’
above.english: I am energetic…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā āraddhavīriyā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, āraddhavīriyataṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who are unmindful and lack situational awareness …
below.english: “‘… unmindful and not fully aware…

above.pali: upaṭṭhitassatihamasmi.
above.sujato: I am mindful …’
above.english: I am established in mindfulness…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā upaṭṭhitassatī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, upaṭṭhitassatitaṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.pali: ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, asamāhitavibbhantacittasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṁ bhayabheravaṁ avhāyanti.
below.sujato: ‘There are ascetics and brahmins who lack immersion, with straying minds …
below.english: “‘…unconcentrated and with straying minds…

above.pali: samādhisampannohamasmi.
above.sujato: I am accomplished in immersion …’
above.english: I am possessed of concentration…’

lines.pali: Ye hi vo ariyā samādhisampannā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṁ aññataro’ti.
Etamahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, samādhisampadaṁ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṁ araññe vihārāya.

below.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi:
below.english: “ I considered thus:

above.pali: ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti—
above.sujato: A mendicant who understands that ill will …
above.english: Knowing that ill will…negligence is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a bhikkhu abandons it.

lines.pali: iti viditvā pamādaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati.

below.pali: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti—iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti,
below.sujato: When they have understood these corruptions of the mind
below.english: “When a bhikkhu has known that covetousness and unrighteous greed is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it;

above.pali: ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti—
above.sujato: for what they are, and have given them up,
above.english: when a bhikkhu has known that ill will…negligence is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it,

iti viditvā sāṭheyyaṁ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti;
iti viditvā thambho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti;

below.pali: So buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
below.sujato: they have experiential confidence in the Buddha:

lines.pali: ‘tathāyaṁ puggalo paṭipanno tathā ca iriyati tañca maggaṁ samārūḷho, yathā āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatī’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘This individual is practicing in such a way and is riding upon such a path that they will realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

lines.pali: Tamenaṁ passāmi aparena samayena āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantaṁ, ekantasukhā vedanā vedayamānaṁ.
lines.sujato: Some time later I see that they have indeed realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements, experiencing feelings of absolute happiness.

above.english: so too, when I saw a cowherd or a shepherd…

above.english: Through feeding on a single rice grain a day, my body reached a state of extreme emaciation.

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma āsītikapabbāni vā kāḷapabbāni vā; evamevassu me aṅgapaccaṅgāni bhavanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma oṭṭhapadaṁ; evamevassu me ānisadaṁ hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma vaṭṭanāvaḷī; evamevassu me piṭṭhikaṇṭako unnatāvanato hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma jarasālāya gopānasiyo oluggaviluggā bhavanti; evamevassu me phāsuḷiyo oluggaviluggā bhavanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma gambhīre udapāne udakatārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti; evamevassu me akkhikūpesu akkhitārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma tittakālābu āmakacchinno vātātapena samphuṭito hoti sammilāto; evamevassu me sīsacchavi samphuṭitā hoti sammilātā tāyevappāhāratāya.

So kho ahaṁ, sāriputta, ‘udaracchaviṁ parimasissāmī’ti piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṁyeva pariggaṇhāmi, ‘piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṁ parimasissāmī’ti udaracchaviṁyeva pariggaṇhāmi. Yāvassu me, sāriputta, udaracchavi piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṁ allīnā hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
So kho ahaṁ, sāriputta, ‘vaccaṁ vā muttaṁ vā karissāmī’ti tattheva avakujjo papatāmi tāyevappāhāratāya.

below.english: Because of eating so little…the hair, rotted at its roots, fell from my body as I rubbed.

lines.pali: “idha mayaṁ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisimha.
yaṁ nūna mayaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodimha;
sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdimha. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho amhe, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṁ:
‘samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapeti, mayampi kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapema.
Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapeti, mayampi rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapema.
Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo vedanānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapeti, mayampi vedanānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapema.
Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṁ nānākaraṇaṁ samaṇassa vā gotamassa amhākaṁ vā, yadidaṁ dhammadesanāya vā dhammadesanaṁ anusāsaniyā vā anusāsanin’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ bhāsitaṁ neva abhinandimha, nappaṭikkosimha;

below.pali: “Evaṁvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā:
below.sujato: “Mendicants, when wanderers of other religions say this, you should say to them:
below.english: “Bhikkhus, wanderers of other sects who speak thus should be questioned thus:

above.pali: So ca kho attabyābādhāyapi saṁvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṁvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṁvattati, paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko’.
above.sujato: It leads to hurting myself, hurting others, and hurting both. It blocks wisdom, it’s on the side of distress, and it doesn’t lead to extinguishment.’
above.english: This leads to my own affliction, to others’ affliction, and to the affliction of both; it obstructs wisdom, causes difficulties, and leads away from Nibbāna.‘

lines.pali: ‘Attabyābādhāya saṁvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṁ gacchati;
lines.sujato: When I reflected that it leads to hurting myself …

lines.pali: ‘parabyābādhāya saṁvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṁ gacchati;
‘ubhayabyābādhāya saṁvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṁ gacchati;

below.pali: ‘paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṁ gacchati.
below.sujato: When I reflected that it blocks wisdom, it’s on the side of distress, and it doesn’t lead to extinguishment, it went away.
below.english: When I considered thus…it subsided in me.

above.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, tassa ce bhikkhuno tamhāpi nimittā aññaṁ nimittaṁ manasikaroto kusalūpasaṁhitaṁ uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṁhitāpi dosūpasaṁhitāpi mohūpasaṁhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṁ vitakkānaṁ ādīnavo upaparikkhitabbo:
above.sujato: In the same way, a mendicant … should examine the drawbacks of those thoughts …
above.english: so too…when a bhikkhu examines the danger in those thoughts…

lines.pali: ‘itipime vitakkā akusalā, itipime vitakkā sāvajjā, itipime vitakkā dukkhavipākā’ti.
Tassa tesaṁ vitakkānaṁ ādīnavaṁ upaparikkhato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṁhitāpi dosūpasaṁhitāpi mohūpasaṁhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.

below.pali: Tesaṁ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṁ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.
below.english: his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.

above.pali: Assosuṁ kho sambahulā bhikkhū:
above.sujato: Several mendicants heard this rumour.
above.english: Several bhikkhus, having heard about this,

lines.pali: “ariṭṭhassa kira nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā’”ti.

below.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū yena ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā ariṭṭhaṁ bhikkhuṁ gaddhabādhipubbaṁ etadavocuṁ:
below.sujato: They went up to Ariṭṭha and said to him,
below.english: went to the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha and asked him:

above.pali: Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu ariṭṭhaṁ bhikkhuṁ gaddhabādhipubbaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: When they weren’t able to dissuade Ariṭṭha from his view, the mendicants went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: Since the bhikkhus were unable to detach him from that pernicious view, they went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side and told him all that had occurred, adding:

lines.pali: “ariṭṭhassa nāma, bhante, bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā’ti.
‘ariṭṭhassa kira nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ—
tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā’ti.

below.pali: Yato kho mayaṁ, bhante, nāsakkhimha ariṭṭhaṁ bhikkhuṁ gaddhabādhipubbaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha mayaṁ etamatthaṁ bhagavato ārocemā”ti.
below.english: “Venerable sir, since we could not detach the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, from this pernicious view, we have reported this matter to the Blessed One.”

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacce moghapurisā dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti—
above.sujato: In the same way, a futile person memorizes the teaching …
above.english: So too, here some misguided men learn the Dhamma…

lines.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Te taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā tesaṁ dhammānaṁ paññāya atthaṁ na upaparikkhanti.
Tesaṁ te dhammā paññāya atthaṁ anupaparikkhataṁ na nijjhānaṁ khamanti.
Te upārambhānisaṁsā ceva dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti itivādappamokkhānisaṁsā ca.
Yassa catthāya dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti tañcassa atthaṁ nānubhonti.
Tesaṁ te dhammā duggahitā dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti.
lines.sujato: and those teachings lead to their lasting harm and suffering.

below.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
below.sujato: Why is that?
below.english: Why is that?

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacce kulaputtā dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti—
above.sujato: In the same way, a gentleman memorizes the teaching …
above.english: So too, here some clansmen learn the Dhamma…

lines.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Te taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā tesaṁ dhammānaṁ paññāya atthaṁ upaparikkhanti.
Tesaṁ te dhammā paññāya atthaṁ upaparikkhataṁ nijjhānaṁ khamanti.
Te na ceva upārambhānisaṁsā dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti, na itivādappamokkhānisaṁsā ca.
Yassa catthāya dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti, tañcassa atthaṁ anubhonti.
Tesaṁ te dhammā suggahitā dīgharattaṁ atthāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattanti.
lines.sujato: and those teachings lead to his lasting welfare and happiness.

below.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
below.sujato: Why is that?
below.english: Why is that?

above.pali: samaṇapaṇḍite nipuṇe kataparappavāde vālavedhirūpe te bhindantā maññe caranti paññāgatena diṭṭhigatāni.
above.sujato: Furthermore, I see some astute ascetics who are subtle, accomplished in the doctrines of others, hair-splitters. …
above.english: “Again, I have seen certain learned recluses who were clever…

lines.pali: ‘samaṇo khalu bho gotamo amukaṁ nāma gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā osarissatī’ti.
Te pañhaṁ abhisaṅkharonti ‘imaṁ mayaṁ pañhaṁ samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma.
Evañce no puṭṭho evaṁ byākarissati, evamassa mayaṁ vādaṁ āropessāma.
Evañcepi no puṭṭho evaṁ byākarissati, evampissa mayaṁ vādaṁ āropessāmā’ti.
Te suṇanti ‘samaṇo khalu bho gotamo amukaṁ nāma gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā osaṭo’ti.
Te samaṇo gotamo dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.

below.pali: Te samaṇena gotamena dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṁsitā na ceva samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ pañhaṁ pucchanti, kutossa vādaṁ āropessanti?
below.sujato: They don’t even get around to asking their question to the ascetic Gotama, so how could they refute his answer?
below.english: They do not so much as ask him the question, so how should they refute his doctrine?

above.pali: Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṁ pare akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesenti.
above.sujato: If others abuse, attack, harass, and trouble that mendicant, they understand:
above.english: “So then, if others abuse, revile, scold, and harass a bhikkhu who has seen this element as it actually is, he understands thus:… repeat §§8—10…

lines.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti, uppannā kho me ayaṁ sotasamphassajā dukkhā vedanā.
lines.sujato: ‘This painful feeling born of ear contact has arisen in me.

lines.pali: Sā ca kho paṭicca, no apaṭicca.
Sopi phasso aniccoti passati, vedanā aniccāti passati, saññā aniccāti passati, saṅkhārā aniccāti passati, viññāṇaṁ aniccanti passati.
lines.sujato: They see that contact, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are impermanent.

lines.pali: Tassa dhātārammaṇameva cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati.
lines.sujato: Based on that element alone, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

below.pali: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno bahukataṁ hoti.
below.sujato: At this point, much has been done by that mendicant.
below.english: At that point too, friends, much has been done by that bhikkhu.

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
above.english: So too, bhikkhus, here some clansman goes forth out of faith…

lines.pali: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto,
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
So evaṁ pabbajito samāno lābhasakkārasilokaṁ abhinibbatteti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena attānukkaṁseti, paraṁ vambheti ‘ahamasmi lābhasakkārasilokavā, ime panaññe bhikkhū appaññātā appesakkhā’ti.

below.pali: So tena lābhasakkārasilokena majjati pamajjati pamādaṁ āpajjati, pamatto samāno dukkhaṁ viharati.
below.english: …he lives in suffering.

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
above.english: So too, bhikkhus, here some clansman goes forth out of faith…he lives in suffering.

lines.pali: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto,
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
So evaṁ pabbajito samāno lābhasakkārasilokaṁ abhinibbatteti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati.
So tāya sīlasampadāya attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya sīlasampadāya attānukkaṁseti, paraṁ vambheti:
‘ahamasmi sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo, ime panaññe bhikkhū dussīlā pāpadhammā’ti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya majjati pamajjati pamādaṁ āpajjati, pamatto samāno dukkhaṁ viharati.

below.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu papaṭikaṁ aggahesi brahmacariyassa;
below.sujato: This is called a mendicant who has grabbed the shoots of the spiritual life
below.english: This bhikkhu is called one who has taken the outer bark of the holy life and stopped short with that.

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
above.english: So too, bhikkhus, here some clansman goes forth out of faith…he lives in suffering.

lines.pali: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto,
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
So evaṁ pabbajito samāno lābhasakkārasilokaṁ abhinibbatteti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno sīlasampadaṁ ārādheti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya attamano hoti no ca kho paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya sīlasampadāya na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno samādhisampadaṁ ārādheti.
So tāya samādhisampadāya attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya samādhisampadāya attānukkaṁseti, paraṁ vambheti:
‘ahamasmi samāhito ekaggacitto, ime panaññe bhikkhū asamāhitā vibbhantacittā’ti.
So tāya samādhisampadāya majjati pamajjati pamādaṁ āpajjati, pamatto samāno dukkhaṁ viharati.

below.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tacaṁ aggahesi brahmacariyassa;
below.sujato: This is called a mendicant who has grabbed the bark of the spiritual life
below.english: This bhikkhu is called one who has taken the inner bark of the holy life and stopped short with that.

above.pali: So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
above.english: He is not pleased with that gain, honour, and renown, and his intention is not fulfilled…

lines.pali: So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati.

below.pali: Appamatto samāno sīlasampadaṁ ārādheti.
below.english: Being diligent, he achieves the attainment of virtue.

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
above.english: So too, bhikkhus, here some clansman goes forth out of faith…he lives in suffering.

lines.pali: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto,
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
So evaṁ pabbajito samāno lābhasakkārasilokaṁ abhinibbatteti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno sīlasampadaṁ ārādheti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya attamano hoti, no ca kho paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya sīlasampadāya na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno samādhisampadaṁ ārādheti.
So tāya samādhisampadāya attamano hoti, no ca kho paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya samādhisampadāya na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tāya samādhisampadāya na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno ñāṇadassanaṁ ārādheti.
So tena ñāṇadassanena attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena ñāṇadassanena attānukkaṁseti, paraṁ vambheti:
‘ahamasmi jānaṁ passaṁ viharāmi, ime panaññe bhikkhū ajānaṁ apassaṁ viharantī’ti.
So tena ñāṇadassanena majjati pamajjati pamādaṁ āpajjati, pamatto samāno dukkhaṁ viharati.

below.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu phegguṁ aggahesi brahmacariyassa;
below.sujato: This is called a mendicant who has grabbed the softwood of the spiritual life
below.english: This bhikkhu is called one who has taken the sapwood of the holy life and stopped short with that.

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
above.english: So too, bhikkhus, here some clansman goes forth out of faith…

appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
So evaṁ pabbajito samāno lābhasakkārasilokaṁ abhinibbatteti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti, na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno sīlasampadaṁ ārādheti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya attamano hoti, no ca kho paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya sīlasampadāya na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tāya sīlasampadāya na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno samādhisampadaṁ ārādheti.
So tāya samādhisampadāya attamano hoti, no ca kho paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tāya samādhisampadāya na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
So tāya samādhisampadāya na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno ñāṇadassanaṁ ārādheti.
So tena ñāṇadassanena attamano hoti, no ca kho paripuṇṇasaṅkappo.
So tena ñāṇadassanena na attānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.

below.pali: So tena ñāṇadassanena na majjati nappamajjati na pamādaṁ āpajjati, appamatto samāno asamayavimokkhaṁ ārādheti.
below.english: When he is diligent, he attains perpetual liberation.

above.pali: Āyasmāpi kho nandiyo …pe…
above.sujato: And the venerables Nandiya and Kimbila spoke likewise, and they added:
above.english: The venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila each spoke likewise, adding:

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ āvi ceva raho ca,
mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ āvi ceva raho ca,
mettaṁ manokammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ āvi ceva raho ca.
‘yannūnāhaṁ sakaṁ cittaṁ nikkhipitvā imesaṁyeva āyasmantānaṁ cittassa vasena vatteyyan’ti.
So kho ahaṁ, bhante, sakaṁ cittaṁ nikkhipitvā imesaṁyeva āyasmantānaṁ cittassa vasena vattāmi.
Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe cittan”ti.

below.pali: “Evaṁ kho mayaṁ, bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṁ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā”ti.
below.sujato: “That’s how we live in harmony, appreciating each other, without quarreling, blending like milk and water, and regarding each other with kindly eyes.”
below.english: “That is how, venerable sir, we are living in concord, with mutual appreciation, without disputing, blending like milk and water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.”

above.pali: “Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, āyasmantaṁ revataṁ etadavocaṁ:
above.sujato: “Next I asked Revata the same question.
above.english: “When this was said, venerable sir, I addressed the venerable Revata thus:

lines.pali: ‘byākataṁ kho, āvuso revata, āyasmatā ānandena yathāsakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ.
Tattha dāni mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ revataṁ pucchāma—

below.pali: ramaṇīyaṁ, āvuso revata, gosiṅgasālavanaṁ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā maññe gandhā sampavanti.
below.english: ‘Friend Revata…

lines.pali: So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṁ viharituṁ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ viharati;
yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṁ viharituṁ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṁ viharati;
yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṁ viharituṁ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṁ viharati.
Seyyathāpi, āvuso moggallāna, rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā nānārattānaṁ dussānaṁ dussakaraṇḍako pūro assa.
So yaññadeva dussayugaṁ ākaṅkheyya pubbaṇhasamayaṁ pārupituṁ, taṁ tadeva dussayugaṁ pubbaṇhasamayaṁ pārupeyya;

lines.pali: “sātissa kira nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’”ti.

below.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū yena sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etadavocuṁ:
below.sujato: They went up to Sāti and said to him,
below.english: went to the bhikkhu Sāti and asked him:

above.pali: Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: When they weren’t able to dissuade Sāti from his view, the mendicants went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: Since the bhikkhus were unable to detach him from that pernicious view, they went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side and told him all that had occurred, adding:

lines.pali: “sātissa nāma, bhante, bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Assumha kho mayaṁ, bhante, sātissa kira nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yena sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etadavocumha:
‘saccaṁ kira te, āvuso sāti, evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan”’ti?
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto amhe etadavoca:
‘evaṁ byā kho ahaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetukāmā samanuyuñjimha samanugāhimha samanubhāsimha:
‘mā evaṁ, āvuso sāti, avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
Anekapariyāyenāvuso sāti, paṭiccasamuppannaṁ viññāṇaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo’ti.
Evampi kho, bhante, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto amhehi samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno tadeva pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ thāmasā parāmasā abhinivissa voharati:
‘evaṁ byā kho ahaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.

below.pali: Yato kho mayaṁ, bhante, nāsakkhimha sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha mayaṁ etamatthaṁ bhagavato ārocemā”ti.
below.english: “Venerable sir, since we could not detach the bhikkhu Sāti, son of a fisherman, from this pernicious view, we have reported this matter to the Blessed One.”

He reveals an entirely full and pure spiritual life.

Etadeva kho pana saṁyojanaṁ etaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ adinnādānaṁ.
Ye ca adinnādānapaccayā uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā adinnādānā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’.

above.english: He does not abide with a mind obsessed and enslaved by doubt…

lines.pali: uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen.
That doubt, along with any underlying tendency to it, is given up in them.

below.pali: Na sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in misapprehension of precepts and observances,
below.english: by adherence to rules and observances…

above.pali: Na sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena;
above.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in misapprehension of precepts and observances,
above.english: by adherence to rules and observances…

lines.pali: uppannassa ca sīlabbataparāmāsassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they truly understand the escape from misapprehension of precepts and observances that has arisen.
That misapprehension of precepts and observances, along with any underlying tendency to it, is given up in them.

below.pali: Na kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na kāmarāgaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in sensual desire,
below.english: by sensual lust…

above.pali: Na kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na kāmarāgaparetena;
above.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in sensual desire,
above.english: by sensual lust…

lines.pali: uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen.
That sensual desire, along with any underlying tendency to it, is given up in them.

below.pali: Na byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na byāpādaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in ill will,
below.english: by ill will;

above.pali: ‘sambahulā kho upāsakā sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasanti, tepi maṁ jānissanti—
above.sujato: several laymen reside in Sāvatthī …
above.english: ‘Many men lay followers…

lines.pali: bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti.
Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosi.
Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi:

below.pali: ‘sambahulā kho upāsikā sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasanti, tāpi maṁ jānissanti—
below.sujato: several laywomen reside in Sāvatthī, and they’ll know me
below.english: Many women lay followers are staying at Sāvatthī, and they too will know me thus:

above.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
above.sujato: Furthermore, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.
above.english: “With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters upon and abides in the second jhāna…

lines.pali: Evañhi taṁ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṁ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.
lines.sujato: Because that’s what happens when someone fulfills the training according to the Teacher’s instructions.

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
below.sujato: Furthermore, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’
below.english: With the fading away as well of rapture…he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna…

above.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

lines.pali: Evañhi taṁ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṁ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.
lines.sujato: Because that’s what happens when someone fulfills the training according to the Teacher’s instructions.

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
below.sujato: Furthermore, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.
below.english: With the abandoning of pleasure and pain…he enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna…

above.pali: Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ hoti:
above.sujato: In such a case, the monks say:
above.english: Bhikkhus, taking account of this matter, think:

lines.sujato: ‘Reverends, this monk is a frequent offender, with many offenses.

lines.pali: So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno aññenaññaṁ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṁ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, na sammā vattati, na lomaṁ pāteti, na netthāraṁ vattati, “yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṁ karomī”ti nāha.
lines.sujato: When admonished by the monks, he dodges the issue, distracting the discussion with irrelevant points. He displays annoyance, hate, and bitterness. He doesn’t proceed properly, he doesn’t fall in line, he doesn’t proceed to get past it, and he doesn’t say: “I’ll do what pleases the Saṅgha.”

below.pali: Sādhu vatāyasmanto imassa bhikkhuno tathā tathā upaparikkhatha yathāssidaṁ adhikaraṇaṁ na khippameva vūpasameyyā’ti.
below.sujato: It’d be good for the venerables to examine this monk in such a way that this disciplinary issue is not quickly settled.’
below.english: ‘It would be good if the venerable ones examine this bhikkhu in such a way that this litigation against him is not settled too quickly.’

above.sujato: In such a case, the monks say:

lines.sujato: When admonished by the monks, he doesn’t dodge the issue, distracting the discussion with irrelevant points. He doesn’t display annoyance, hate, and bitterness. He proceeds properly, he falls in line, he proceeds to get past it, and he says: “I’ll do what pleases the Saṅgha.”

below.pali: Sādhu vatāyasmanto, imassa bhikkhuno tathā tathā upaparikkhatha yathāssidaṁ adhikaraṇaṁ khippameva vūpasameyyā’ti.
below.sujato: It’d be good for the venerables to examine this monk in such a way that this disciplinary issue is quickly settled.’
below.english: ‘It would be good if the venerable ones examine this bhikkhu in such a way that this litigation against him is settled quickly.’

above.pali: So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno aññenaññaṁ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṁ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, na sammā vattati, na lomaṁ pāteti, na netthāraṁ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṁ karomī’ti nāha.
above.sujato: When admonished by the monks, he dodges the issue …
above.english: When he is corrected by the bhikkhus, he prevaricates…

lines.sujato: In such a case, the monks say:
‘Reverends, this monk is an occasional offender without many offenses.

above.pali: evameva kho, bhaddāli, idhekacco bhikkhu saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakena.
above.sujato: In the same way, some monk gets by with mere faith and fondness.
above.english: So too, some bhikkhu progresses by a measure of faith and love…

lines.sujato: In such a case, the monks say:

lines.pali: ‘ayaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakena.
lines.sujato: ‘Reverends, this monk gets by with mere faith and fondness.

lines.pali: Sace mayaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṁ karissāma—
lines.sujato: Suppose we punish him, repeatedly pressuring him—

below.pali: mā yampissa taṁ saddhāmattakaṁ pemamattakaṁ tamhāpi parihāyī’ti.
below.sujato: no, let him not lose what little faith and love he has!’
below.english: ‘Let him not lose that measure of faith and love, as he may if we take action against him by repeatedly admonishing him.’

above.pali: Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū saññāpetuṁ, atha yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Since those mendicants were unable to persuade the mendicants who were followers of Assaji and Punabbasuka, they approached the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: Since the bhikkhus were unable to convince the bhikkhus led by Assaji and Punabbasuka, they went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to him, they sat down at one side and told him all that had occurred, adding:

lines.pali: “idha mayaṁ, bhante, yena assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū etadavocumha:
‘bhagavā kho, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjati bhikkhusaṅgho ca;
aññatra kho panāvuso, rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānanti appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca.
Etha, tumhepi, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha.
Aññatra kho panāvuso, tumhepi rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū amhe etadavocuṁ:
‘mayaṁ kho, āvuso, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle.
Te mayaṁ sāyañceva bhuñjamānā pāto ca divā ca vikāle appābādhatañca sañjānāma appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca.
Te mayaṁ kiṁ sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvissāma?
Sāyañceva mayaṁ bhuñjissāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle’ti.

below.pali: Yato kho mayaṁ, bhante, nāsakkhimha assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū saññāpetuṁ, atha mayaṁ etamatthaṁ bhagavato ārocemā”ti.
below.english: “Venerable sir, since we were unable to convince the bhikkhus led by Assaji and Punabbasuka, we have reported this matter to the Blessed One.”

above.pali: Mayā cetaṁ, bhikkhave, aññātaṁ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṁ aviditaṁ asacchikataṁ aphassitaṁ paññāya:
above.sujato: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:
above.english: “If it were unknown by me…

lines.pali: ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evāhaṁ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ pajahathā’ti vadeyyaṁ;
lines.sujato: ‘When someone feels this kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’

lines.pali: api nu me etaṁ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṁ abhavissā”ti?
lines.sujato: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should give up this kind of painful feeling’?”

below.pali: “Yasmā ca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, mayā ñātaṁ diṭṭhaṁ viditaṁ sacchikataṁ phassitaṁ paññāya:
below.sujato: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:
below.english: But because it is known by me…contacted by wisdom thus:

above.pali: jivhā kho, māgaṇḍiya, rasārāmā rasaratā rasasammuditā.
above.sujato: The tongue likes tastes …
above.english: The tongue delights in flavours…

lines.pali: Sā tathāgatassa dantā guttā rakkhitā saṁvutā, tassā ca saṁvarāya dhammaṁ deseti.
Idaṁ nu te etaṁ, māgaṇḍiya, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
“Etadeva kho pana me, bho gotama, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:

below.pali: “Kāyo kho, māgaṇḍiya, phoṭṭhabbārāmo phoṭṭhabbarato …pe…
below.sujato: The body likes touches …
below.english: The body delights in tangibles…

above.pali: “Evameva kho ahaṁ, māgaṇḍiya, pubbe agāriyabhūto samāno pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāresiṁ cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṁhitehi rajanīyehi, sotaviññeyyehi saddehi …pe…
above.sujato: “In the same way, Māgaṇḍiya, when I was still a layperson I used to amuse myself with sights … sounds …
above.english: “So too, Māgandiya, formerly when I lived the home life, I enjoyed myself, provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure: with forms cognizable by the eye…

below.pali: kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṁhitehi rajanīyehi.
below.sujato: touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
below.english: with tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

above.pali: “Evameva kho ahaṁ, māgaṇḍiya, pubbe agāriyabhūto samāno pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāresiṁ, cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṁhitehi rajanīyehi, sotaviññeyyehi saddehi …pe…

above.english: “So too, Māgandiya, formerly when I lived the home life…as in §12…

lines.sujato: touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

lines.pali: So aparena samayena kāmānaṁyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā kāmataṇhaṁ pahāya kāmapariḷāhaṁ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṁ vūpasantacitto viharāmi.
lines.sujato: Some time later—having truly understood the origin, ending, gratification, drawback, and escape of sensual pleasures, and having given up craving and dispelled passion for sensual pleasures—I live rid of thirst, my mind settled internally.

lines.pali: So aññe satte passāmi kāmesu avītarāge kāmataṇhāhi khajjamāne kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamāne kāme paṭisevante.
lines.sujato: I see other sentient beings who are not free from sensual pleasures being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with passion for sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures.

lines.pali: So tesaṁ na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi.
lines.sujato: I don’t envy them, nor do I hope to enjoy that.

lines.pali: Yāhayaṁ, māgaṇḍiya, rati, aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi—
lines.sujato: Because there is a satisfaction that is apart from sensual pleasures and unskillful qualities,

below.pali: tāya ratiyā ramamāno hīnassa na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi.
below.sujato: Enjoying that satisfaction, I don’t envy what is inferior, nor do I hope to enjoy it.
below.english: Since I take delight in that, I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight therein.

above.pali: so ca kho sāvakānaṁ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
above.sujato: But he’s not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. And his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.
above.english: but he is not honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

lines.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṁ deseti.
lines.sujato: Once it so happened that he was teaching an assembly of many hundreds.
Then one of his disciples made a noise,
“My good fellows, don’t ask the Jain Ñātika about that.
I know it. Ask me about it,

lines.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto bāhā paggayha kandanto na labhati:
lines.sujato: Once it so happened that the Jain Ñātika didn’t get his way, though he called out with raised arms,
“Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

lines.pali: Nete bhavante pucchanti, amhe ete pucchanti;
lines.sujato: They’re not asking you, they’re asking me!

lines.pali: Bahū kho pana nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā vādaṁ āropetvā apakkantā:
lines.sujato: Indeed, many of his disciples have left him after refuting his doctrine:

lines.pali: “na tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāsi, ahaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāmi. Kiṁ tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānissasi? Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi. Ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṁ me asahitaṁ te, purevacanīyaṁ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṁ pure avaca, adhiciṇṇaṁ te viparāvattaṁ, āropito te vādo, niggahitosi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī”ti.
lines.sujato: “You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. I stay on topic, you don’t. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!”

lines.pali: Iti nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṁ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
lines.sujato: That’s how the Jain Ñātika is not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. On the contrary, his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

below.pali: Akkuṭṭho ca pana nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto dhammakkosenā’ti.
below.sujato: Rather, he’s reviled, and rightly so.’
below.english: Indeed, he is scorned by the scorn shown to his Dhamma.’

above.pali: sappāṭihāriyaṁ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no appāṭihāriyan’ti.
above.sujato: He teaches with a demonstrable basis, not without it.’
above.english: he teaches the Dhamma in a convincing manner, not in an unconvincing manner.’

lines.pali: Yampudāyi, mamaṁ sāvakā abhikkante ñāṇadassane sambhāventi:
abhiññāya samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no anabhiññāya;
sanidānaṁ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no anidānaṁ;

below.pali: sappāṭihāriyaṁ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no appāṭihāriyan’ti, ayaṁ kho, udāyi, dutiyo dhammo yena mamaṁ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
below.sujato: this is the second quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.
below.english: This is the second quality because of which my disciples honour me…

above.pali: dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ ariyasaccaṁ pucchanti, tesāhaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ ariyasaccaṁ puṭṭho byākaromi, tesāhaṁ cittaṁ ārādhemi pañhassa veyyākaraṇena.
above.sujato: and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering apply to the suffering  in which they are swamped and mired. And I provide them with satisfying answers to their questions.
above.english: about the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering. Being asked, I explain to them the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation.

lines.pali: Yampudāyi, mama sāvakā yena dukkhena dukkhotiṇṇā dukkhaparetā te maṁ upasaṅkamitvā dukkhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ pucchanti, tesāhaṁ dukkhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ puṭṭho byākaromi, tesāhaṁ cittaṁ ārādhemi pañhassa veyyākaraṇena.
Tesāhaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ ariyasaccaṁ puṭṭho byākaromi.

below.pali: Ayaṁ kho, udāyi, catuttho dhammo yena mamaṁ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
below.sujato: this is the fourth quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.
below.english: This is the fourth quality because of which my disciples honour me…

above.pali: evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṁ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānanti—
above.sujato: In the same way, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind …
above.english: so too, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way to understand…an unliberated mind as unliberated.

below.pali: Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
below.sujato: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.
below.english: And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

above.pali: “ammatātā, yathā yathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, nayidaṁ sukaraṁ agāraṁ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṁ ekantaparisuddhaṁ saṅkhalikhitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ carituṁ.
above.english: “Mother and father…give me permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.”

lines.pali: Icchāmahaṁ kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajituṁ.

below.pali: Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṁ kulaputtaṁ etadavocuṁ:
below.english: For the third time his parents replied:

above.pali: “tvaṁ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṁ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato.
above.english: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla…how could we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?”

lines.pali: Na tvaṁ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi.
Maraṇenapi te mayaṁ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma.

below.pali: Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto:
below.sujato: Then Raṭṭhapāla thought,
below.english: Then, not receiving his parents’ permission to go forth,

above.pali: Na tvaṁ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci, dukkhassa jānāsi.
above.sujato: You know nothing of suffering.
above.english: you know nothing of suffering, dear Raṭṭhapāla.

lines.pali: Maraṇenapi te mayaṁ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma.
lines.sujato: When you die we will lose you against our wishes.

lines.pali: Kiṁ pana mayaṁ taṁ jīvantaṁ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjāya.
lines.sujato: So how can we allow you to go forth from lay life to homelessness while you’re still living?

below.pali: Uṭṭhehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca;
below.sujato: Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Eat, drink, and amuse yourself.
below.english: Get up, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and amuse yourself.

below.pali: Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi.
below.sujato: And for a third time, Raṭṭhapāla kept silent. Raṭṭhapāla’s parents then went to see his friends. They told them of the situation and asked for their help.
below.english: For the third time the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent. Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s parents went to his friends and said to them: “Dears, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla has lain down on the bare floor, having said: ‘Right here I shall either die or receive the going forth.’ Come, dears, go to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla and say to him: ‘Friend Raṭṭhapāla, you are your parents’ only son…Get up, friend Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and amuse yourself… how could your parents give you their permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’”

above.pali: Na tvaṁ, samma raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi.
above.sujato: You know nothing of suffering.
above.english: you know nothing of suffering, friend Raṭṭhapāla.

lines.sujato: When you die your parents will lose you against their wishes.

above.english: “Friend Raṭṭhapāla…how could they give you their permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?”

Uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu.
