above.english: and there I saw a large country, powerful and rich…Conquer it then, great king.’

lines.pali: Bahū tattha hatthikāyā assakāyā rathakāyā pattikāyā;

below.pali: Abhivijina, mahārājā’ti, kinti naṁ kareyyāsī”ti?
below.sujato: What would you do?”
below.english: What would you do?”

above.pali: “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ opāsādaṁ anuppatto, opāsāde viharati uttarena opāsādaṁ devavane sālavane.
above.sujato: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Opāsāda together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants. He is staying in the Godswood to the north.
above.english: “The recluse Gotama…as MN91,

lines.pali: Taṁ kho pana bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ evaṁ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato:
‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

lines.pali: So imaṁ lokaṁ sadevakaṁ samārakaṁ sabrahmakaṁ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṁ pajaṁ sadevamanussaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti.
lines.sujato: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

lines.pali: So dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
lines.sujato: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

below.pali: Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṁ arahataṁ dassanaṁ hotī”ti.
below.sujato: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

above.sujato: “Yes, worthy sir,” replied the butler, and did as he was asked.
above.english: “Yes, sir,” the minister replied, and he went to the brahmin householders of Opasāda and gave them the message.

below.sujato: Now at that time around five hundred brahmins from abroad were residing in Opāsāda on some business.
below.english: Now on that occasion five hundred brahmins from various states were staying at Opasāda for some business or other.

lines.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā sati hoti asammuṭṭhā, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, satisambojjhaṅgaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.
lines.sujato: At such a time, a mendicant has initiated the awakening factor of mindfulness …

lines.pali: So tathāsato viharanto taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinati pavicayati parivīmaṁsaṁ āpajjati.

Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāsato viharanto taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinati pavicayati parivīmaṁsaṁ āpajjati, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.
Tassa taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinato pavicayato parivīmaṁsaṁ āpajjato āraddhaṁ hoti vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ.

Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinato pavicayato parivīmaṁsaṁ āpajjato āraddhaṁ hoti vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.

Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā, pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, pītisambojjhaṅgaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.

Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.

Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati, samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, samādhisambojjhaṅgaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.
So tathāsamāhitaṁ cittaṁ sādhukaṁ ajjhupekkhitā hoti.

lines.pali: Sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto attadutiyo yena rājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
Addasaṁsu kho tā bhikkhuniyo āyasmantaṁ nandakaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
Disvāna āsanaṁ paññāpesuṁ, udakañca pādānaṁ upaṭṭhapesuṁ.
Nisīdi kho āyasmā nandako paññatte āsane.
Tāpi kho bhikkhuniyo āyasmantaṁ nandakaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho tā bhikkhuniyo āyasmā nandako etadavoca:
Tattha ājānantīhi ‘ājānāmā’ tissa vacanīyaṁ, na ājānantīhi ‘na ājānāmā’ tissa vacanīyaṁ.
Yassā vā panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, ahameva tattha paṭipucchitabbo:
“Ettakenapi mayaṁ, bhante, ayyassa nandakassa attamanā abhiraddhā yaṁ no ayyo nandako pavāretī”ti.

lines.pali: So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
lines.sujato: When you experience a pleasant feeling, if you approve, welcome, and keep clinging to it,
the underlying tendency to greed underlies that.

lines.pali: Dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṁ kandati sammohaṁ āpajjati.
lines.sujato: When you experience a painful feeling, if you sorrow and wail and lament, beating your breast and falling into confusion,
the underlying tendency to aversion underlies that.

lines.pali: Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno tassā vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
lines.sujato: When you experience a neutral feeling, if you don’t truly understand that feeling’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape,
the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies that.

below.pali: So vata, bhikkhave, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayaṁ appahāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayaṁ appaṭivinodetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayaṁ asamūhanitvā avijjaṁ appahāya vijjaṁ anuppādetvā diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro bhavissatīti—netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
below.sujato: Mendicants, without giving up the underlying tendency to greed for pleasant feeling, without dispelling the underlying tendency to aversion toward painful feeling, without eradicating ignorance in the case of neutral feeling, without giving up ignorance and without giving rise to knowledge, it is quite impossible to make an end of suffering in this very life.
below.english: Bhikkhus, that one should here and now make an end of suffering without abandoning the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling…without abandoning ignorance and arousing true knowledge—this is impossible.

above.pali: “Manañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā.
above.sujato: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact. Contact is a requirement for what is felt as pleasant, painful, or neutral.
above.english: Dependent on the mind and mind-objects, mind-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition there arises a feeling felt as pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant…

lines.pali: So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
lines.sujato: When you experience a pleasant feeling, if you don’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to it,
the underlying tendency to greed does not underlie that.

lines.pali: Dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati na kilamati na paridevati na urattāḷiṁ kandati na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
lines.sujato: When you experience a painful feeling, if you don’t sorrow or wail or lament, beating your breast and falling into confusion,
the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie that.

lines.pali: Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno tassā vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
lines.sujato: When you experience a neutral feeling, if you truly understand that feeling’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape,
the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie that.

below.pali: So vata, bhikkhave, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayaṁ pahāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayaṁ paṭivinodetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayaṁ samūhanitvā avijjaṁ pahāya vijjaṁ uppādetvā diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro bhavissatīti—ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
below.sujato: Mendicants, after giving up the underlying tendency to greed for pleasant feeling, after dispelling the underlying tendency to aversion toward painful feeling, after eradicating ignorance in the case of neutral feeling, after giving up ignorance and giving rise to knowledge, it’s quite possible to make an end of suffering in this very life.
below.english: Bhikkhus, that one shall here and now make an end of suffering by abandoning the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling…by abandoning ignorance and arousing true knowledge—this is possible.

above.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Then those mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said,
above.english: Then those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported everything in full. The Blessed One said:

lines.pali: “idha mayaṁ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāma.
Atha kho, bhante, aññataro brāhmaṇo mahantena jaṭaṇḍuvena ajinakkhipanivattho jiṇṇo gopānasivaṅko ghurughurupassāsī udumbaradaṇḍaṁ gahetvā yena mayaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā amhe etadavoca:
‘daharā bhavanto pabbajitā susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikkīḷitāvino kāmesu.
Evaṁ vutte, mayaṁ, bhante, taṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavocumha:
‘na kho mayaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvāma.
Kālikañca kho mayaṁ, brāhmaṇa, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṁ anudhāvāma.
Kālikā hi, brāhmaṇa, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, so brāhmaṇo sīsaṁ okampetvā jivhaṁ nillāletvā tivisākhaṁ nalāṭe nalāṭikaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkanto”ti.

below.pali: “Neso, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇo.
below.sujato: “Mendicants, that was no brahmin.
below.english: “That was not a brahmin, bhikkhus.

above.pali: Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno āyasmā samiddhi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then Samiddhi went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said,
above.english: Then the Venerable Samiddhi approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported what had happened. The Blessed One said:

lines.pali: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharāmi.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, avidūre mahābhayabheravasaddo ahosi, apissudaṁ pathavī maññe undrīyatī”ti.

below.pali: “Nesā, samiddhi, pathavī undrīyati.
below.sujato: “Samiddhi, that’s not the earth shattering.
below.english: “That was not the earth splitting open, Samiddhi.

above.pali: Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi:
above.sujato: For a third time Sakka addressed Suvīra,
above.english: A third time Sakka addressed Suvīra …

lines.sujato: ‘Dear Suvīra, the titans march against the gods!
Go, and march against the titans!’

below.pali: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā tatiyampi pamādaṁ āpādesi.
below.sujato: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Suvīra. But for a third time he fell into negligence.
below.english: but a third time Suvīra became negligent.

above.pali: ‘idha te, mārisa, aññataro yakkho dubbaṇṇo okoṭimako sakkassa devānamindassa āsane nisinno.
above.english: ‘Here, dear sir, an ugly deformed yakkha has sat down on your seat….

lines.pali: Tatra sudaṁ, mārisa, devā tāvatiṁsā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti:
Ayaṁ yakkho dubbaṇṇo okoṭimako sakkassa devānamindassa āsane nisinno”ti.

below.pali: Yathā yathā kho, mārisa, devā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti tathā tathā so yakkho abhirūpataro ceva hoti dassanīyataro ca pāsādikataro cāti.
below.english: But to whatever extent the devas found fault with this … that yakkha became more and more handsome, more and more comely, more and more graceful.’—

above.pali: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported to him what had happened.

lines.pali: “idha, bhante, dve bhikkhū sampayojesuṁ, tatreko bhikkhu accasarā.
Atha kho so, bhante, bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno santike accayaṁ accayato deseti, so bhikkhu nappaṭiggaṇhātī”ti.

below.pali: “Dveme, bhikkhave, bālā.
below.sujato: “Mendicants, there are two fools.
below.english: The Blessed One said: “Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of fools:

above.pali: saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṁ;
above.sujato: Choices are a requirement for consciousness.
above.english: with volitional formations, consciousness …

lines.sujato: Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.

below.pali: phassapaccayā vedanā;
below.sujato: Contact is a requirement for feeling.
below.english: as in preceding sutta …

above.pali: phassapaccayā vedanā;
above.sujato: Contact is a requirement for feeling.
above.english: as in preceding sutta …

lines.sujato: Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

below.pali: Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.
below.sujato: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
below.english: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

above.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
above.sujato: Then Vipassī thought:

lines.pali: ‘kimhi nu kho sati bhavo hoti, kiṁpaccayā bhavo’ti?
lines.sujato: ‘When what exists is there continued existence? What is a requirement for continued existence?’

lines.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
lines.sujato: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

lines.pali: ‘upādāne kho sati bhavo hoti, upādānapaccayā bhavo’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘When grasping exists there’s continued existence. Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.’

below.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
below.sujato: Then Vipassī thought:

above.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
above.sujato: Then Vipassī thought:

lines.pali: ‘kimhi nu kho sati taṇhā hoti, kiṁpaccayā taṇhā’ti?
lines.sujato: ‘When what exists is there craving? What is a requirement for craving?’

lines.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
lines.sujato: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

lines.pali: ‘vedanāya kho sati taṇhā hoti, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘When feeling exists there’s craving. Feeling is a requirement for craving.’

below.pali: Iti hidaṁ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā;
below.sujato: And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.

above.pali: jātiṁ …pe…
above.sujato: They understand rebirth …
above.english: who understand birth …

below.pali: saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti,
below.sujato: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.
below.english: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation:

above.pali: jātiṁ …pe…
above.sujato: They understand rebirth …
above.english: They understand birth …

below.pali: saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti.
below.sujato: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.
below.english: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation.

above.sujato: If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment regarding rebirth …
above.english: “Bhikkhu, if one teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of revulsion towards birth …

below.pali: avijjāya ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
below.sujato: If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding ignorance, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.
below.english: for the purpose of revulsion towards ignorance, for its fading away and cessation, one is fit to be called a bhikkhu who is a speaker on the Dhamma.

above.pali: antaragharaṁ paviṭṭhamhā”ti.
above.english: We have entered among the houses.”

lines.sujato: and a third time, Kassapa spoke to the Buddha and the Buddha replied.

below.pali: Evaṁ vutte, acelo kassapo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
below.sujato: When this was said, Kassapa said to the Buddha,
below.english: Then the naked ascetic Kassapa said to the Blessed One:

above.pali: ‘iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo,
above.sujato: Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.
above.english: ‘Such is form …

lines.pali: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo,
lines.sujato: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the disappearance of feeling.

lines.pali: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo,
lines.sujato: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the disappearance of perception.

lines.pali: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo,
lines.sujato: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the disappearance of choices.

lines.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo.
lines.sujato: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.

below.pali: Yadidaṁ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā;
below.sujato: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
below.english: as in §21 …

above.pali: Tatrānanda, yepi te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkataṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti, te vata aññatra phassā paṭisaṁvedissantīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
above.sujato: In the case of those who assert that suffering is made by oneself, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact. …
above.english: “Therein, Ānanda, in the case of those ascetics and brahmins, proponents of kamma, who maintain that suffering is created by oneself …

below.pali: yepi te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti, te vata aññatra phassā paṭisaṁvedissantīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
below.sujato: In the case of those who assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.
below.english: and those who maintain that suffering has arisen fortuitously, being created neither by oneself nor by another, it is impossible that they will experience anything without contact.

above.pali: ‘Santāvuso gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkataṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
above.sujato: (The wanderers asked the Buddha the very same questions, and he gave the same answers.)
above.english: The wanderers then said to me as I was sitting to one side: … the wanderers ask exactly the same question as they had asked Sāriputta and receive an identical reply …

lines.pali: Santi panāvuso gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā paraṅkataṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
Santāvuso gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
Santi panāvuso gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
Idha no āyasmā gotamo kiṁvādī kimakkhāyī?

Kathaṁ byākaramānā ca mayaṁ vuttavādino ceva āyasmato gotamassa assāma, na ca āyasmantaṁ gotamaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākareyyāma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānupāto gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgaccheyyā’ti?

below.pali: yepi te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti, te vata aññatra phassā paṭisaṁvedissantīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatī’”ti.
below.english: it is impossible that they will experience anything without contact.”

above.pali: vedanā panāvuso …pe…
above.sujato: feeling …
above.english: Feeling has contact as its source …

lines.sujato: Suppose they were to ask me:

lines.pali: ‘phasso panāvuso ānanda, kiṁnidāno kiṁsamudayo kiṁjātiko kiṁpabhavo’ti?

below.pali: ‘phasso kho, āvuso, saḷāyatananidāno saḷāyatanasamudayo saḷāyatanajātiko saḷāyatanappabhavo’ti.
below.sujato: ‘The six sense fields are the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of contact.’
below.english: Contact has the six sense bases as its source, the six sense bases as its origin; it is born and produced from the six sense bases.

above.pali: Tatrānanda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkataṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti tadapi phassapaccayā.
above.sujato: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, that’s dependent on contact. …
above.english: “Therein, Ānanda, in the case of those ascetics and brahmins, proponents of kamma, who maintain that pleasure and pain are created by oneself …

below.pali: yepi te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti tadapi phassapaccayā.
below.sujato: In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another, that’s also dependent on contact.
below.english: and those who maintain that pleasure and pain have arisen fortuitously … in each case that is conditioned by contact.

above.pali: Tatrānanda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkataṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti, te vata aññatra phassā paṭisaṁvedissantīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
above.sujato: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact. …
above.english: “Therein, Ānanda, in the case of those ascetics and brahmins, proponents of kamma, who maintain that pleasure and pain are created by oneself …

below.pali: yepi te samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti, te vata aññatra phassā paṭisaṁvedissantīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
below.sujato: In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.
below.english: and those who maintain that pleasure and pain have arisen fortuitously … in each case it is impossible that they will experience anything without contact.

above.pali: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṁ pāliccaṁ valittacatā āyuno saṁhāni indriyānaṁ paripāko—
above.sujato: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.
above.english: The aging of the various beings …

lines.pali: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṁ maccu maraṇaṁ kālakiriyā khandhānaṁ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo;
lines.sujato: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

below.pali: idaṁ vuccati maraṇaṁ.
below.sujato: This is called death.
below.english: as in §2 …

above.pali: Katamañca, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṁ?
above.sujato: And what is old age and death?
above.english: “And what, bhikkhus, is aging-and-death?…

lines.pali: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṁ pāliccaṁ valittacatā āyuno saṁhāni indriyānaṁ paripāko—
lines.sujato: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

lines.pali: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṁ maccu maraṇaṁ kālakiriyā khandhānaṁ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo;
lines.sujato: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.
Such is old age, and such is death.
This is called old age and death.
Rebirth is the origin of old age and death.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.

below.pali: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminī paṭipadā.
below.sujato: The practice that leads to the cessation of old age and death is simply this noble eightfold path,
below.english: as in preceding sutta …

above.pali: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṁ parijānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṁ parijānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṁ parijānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ parijānanti, jātiṁ parijānanti …pe…
above.sujato: There are ascetics and brahmins who completely understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. They completely understand rebirth …
above.english: “But, bhikkhus, those ascetics and brahmins who fully understand aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation; who fully understand birth …

below.pali: saṅkhāre parijānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ parijānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ parijānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ parijānanti.
below.sujato: They completely understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.
below.english: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation:

above.pali: Jātiṁ pajānanti …pe…
above.sujato: They understand rebirth …
above.english: As to those ascetics and brahmins who understand birth …

below.pali: saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti.
below.sujato: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.
below.english: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation:

above.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, bhūtamidanti, sāriputta, yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
above.sujato: “Good, good, Sāriputta! (The Buddha repeated all of Sāriputta’s explanation, concluding:)
above.english: “Good, good, Sāriputta!… the Buddha repeats here the entire statement of the Venerable Sāriputta …

lines.pali: Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

below.pali: Imassa kho, sāriputta, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
below.sujato: This is how to see the detailed meaning of what was said in brief.”
below.english: it is in such a way that the meaning of this, stated in brief, should be understood in detail.”

above.pali: “Sace maṁ, bhante, evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,
above.english: “If they were to ask me this, venerable sir,

khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti;

below.pali: evaṁ puṭṭhohaṁ, bhante, evaṁ byākareyyaṁ:
below.sujato: I would answer:
below.english: I would answer thus:

above.pali: “Sace maṁ, bhante, evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,
above.english: “If they were to ask me this, venerable sir,

lines.pali: ‘kathaṁ vimokkhā pana tayā, āvuso sāriputta, aññā byākatā—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.

below.pali: Evaṁ puṭṭhohaṁ, bhante, evaṁ byākareyyaṁ:
below.sujato: I’d answer:
below.english: I would answer thus:

above.pali: Yato ca kho me, āvuso, bhagavā paṭhamaṁ pañhaṁ anumodi, tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi—
above.english: But when the Blessed One approved of my answer, it occurred to me:

lines.pali: divasañcepi maṁ bhagavā etamatthaṁ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, divasampāhaṁ bhagavato etamatthaṁ byākareyyaṁ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi;

below.pali: satta rattindivāni cepi maṁ bhagavā etamatthaṁ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, satta rattindivānipāhaṁ bhagavato etamatthaṁ byākareyyaṁ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehī”ti.
below.english: “If the Blessed One were to question me about this matter for up to seven days and nights, for up to seven days and nights I would be able to answer him with various terms and with various methods.”’”

above.pali: “Sā hi, bhikkhu, sāriputtassa dhammadhātu suppaṭividdhā, yassā dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā divasaṁ cepāhaṁ sāriputtaṁ etamatthaṁ puccheyyaṁ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, divasampi me sāriputto etamatthaṁ byākareyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi.
above.sujato: “Mendicant, Sāriputta has clearly penetrated the principle of the teachings, so that he could answer any questions I might ask him in different words and ways up to the seventh day and night.”
above.english: “Bhikkhu, the Venerable Sāriputta has thoroughly penetrated that element of the Dhamma by the thorough penetration of which, if I were to question him about that matter with various terms and with various methods for up to seven days and nights, for up to seven days and nights he would be able to answer me with various terms and with various methods.”

above.sujato: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.
above.english: definition as in §2 …

lines.pali: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṁ maccu maraṇaṁ kālakiriyā khandhānaṁ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo.
lines.sujato: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

above.pali: “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca, “‘katamā jāti, kassa ca panāyaṁ jātī’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ‘aññā jāti aññassa ca panāyaṁ jātī’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṁ ekatthaṁ byañjanameva nānaṁ.
above.sujato: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha. “You might say, ‘What is rebirth, and who does it belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Rebirth is one thing, who it belongs to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.
above.english: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied. “Bhikkhu, whether one says, ‘What now is birth, and for whom is there this birth?’ or whether one says, ‘Birth is one thing, the one for whom there is this birth is another’—both these assertions are identical in meaning; they differ only in the phrasing….

lines.pali: Taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.
lines.sujato: Mendicant, if you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

lines.pali: Aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.
lines.sujato: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

below.pali: Ete te, bhikkhu, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
below.sujato: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
below.english: Without veering towards either of these extremes, the Tathagata teaches the Dhamma by the middle:

above.pali: “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca, “‘katamo bhavo, kassa ca panāyaṁ bhavo’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ‘añño bhavo aññassa ca panāyaṁ bhavo’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṁ ekatthaṁ byañjanameva nānaṁ.
above.sujato: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha. “You might say, ‘What is continued existence, and who does it belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Continued existence is one thing, who it belongs to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.
above.english: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied. “Bhikkhu, whether one says, ‘What now is existence, and for whom is there this existence?’ or whether one says, ‘Existence is one thing, the one for whom there is this existence is another’—both these assertions are identical in meaning; they differ only in the phrasing….

lines.pali: Taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti;

above.sujato: Mendicants, you might say, ‘What are old age and death, and who do they belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Old age and death are one thing, who they belong to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.
above.english: This sutta is identical with the preceding one, differing only in that the bhikkhus are addressed collectively throughout, and there is no interlocutor who asks inappropriate questions.

lines.pali: ‘Taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.

above.pali: Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti.
above.sujato: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.
above.english: When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishing of consciousness….

lines.pali: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti.
lines.sujato: When consciousness is established and grows, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

lines.pali: Āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā sati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti.
lines.sujato: When there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

below.pali: Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.
below.sujato: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
below.english: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

above.pali: Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti.
above.sujato: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

lines.pali: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nati hoti.
lines.sujato: When consciousness is established and grows, there is an inclination.
When there is an inclination, there is coming and going.
When there is coming and going, there is passing away and reappearing.

lines.pali: Cutūpapāte sati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti.
lines.sujato: When there is passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

above.sujato: When consciousness exists name and form come to be.
above.english: When there is consciousness, name-and-form comes to be….

lines.sujato: When name and form exist the six sense fields come to be.
When the six sense fields exist contact comes to be.
When contact exists feeling comes to be.
When feeling exists craving comes to be.
When craving exists grasping comes to be.
When grasping exists continued existence comes to be.
When continued existence exists rebirth comes to be.

below.pali: jātiyā sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hotī’ti.
below.sujato: When rebirth exists old age and death come to be.’
below.english: When there is birth, aging-and-death comes to be.’

continued existence doesn’t come to be …

above.english: ‘What is the source of this birth, what is its origin, from what is it born and produced?…

lines.sujato: While making an inquiry they understand:
‘Continued existence is the source of rebirth.

lines.pali: bhave sati jāti hoti, bhave asati jāti na hotī’ti.
lines.sujato: When continued existence exists, rebirth comes to be. When continued existence does not exist, rebirth doesn’t come to be.’

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, saṁyojaniyesu dhammesu assādānupassino viharato taṇhā pavaḍḍhati.

above.english: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, craving increases….

lines.sujato: Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

below.pali: Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

above.sujato: In the same way, there are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, your craving ceases.
above.english: “So too, bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases….

lines.sujato: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …

below.pali: evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti.

lines.pali: So taṁ rukkhaṁ mūle chindeyya, mūle chetvā palikhaṇeyya, palikhaṇitvā mūlāni uddhareyya …pe…
lines.sujato: They’d cut the tree down at the roots, dig them up, and pull them out, down to the fibers and stems.

They’d cut the tree apart, cut up the parts, and chop it into splinters. They’d dry the splinters in the wind and sun, burn them with fire, and reduce them to ashes. Then they’d winnow the ashes in a strong wind, or glide them down a swift stream.

lines.pali: Evañhi so, bhikkhave, mahārukkho ucchinnamūlo assa tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo.
lines.sujato: In this way the great tree is cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

lines.sujato: Where choices don’t grow, there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

lines.pali: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, natthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
lines.sujato: Where there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

above.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci atītamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ aniccato addakkhuṁ dukkhato addakkhuṁ anattato addakkhuṁ rogato addakkhuṁ bhayato addakkhuṁ,
above.sujato: In the same way, there were ascetics and brahmins of the past who saw the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self, as diseased, and as dangerous.
above.english: “So too, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics and brahmins in the past …

lines.pali: Ye taṇhaṁ pajahiṁsu te upadhiṁ pajahiṁsu.
lines.sujato: Giving up craving, they gave up attachments.

lines.pali: Ye upadhiṁ pajahiṁsu te dukkhaṁ pajahiṁsu.
lines.sujato: Giving up attachments, they gave up suffering.

lines.pali: Ye dukkhaṁ pajahiṁsu te parimucciṁsu jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimucciṁsu dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
lines.sujato: Giving up suffering, they were freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They were freed from suffering, I say.

above.english: ‘With existence as condition, birth’?…

lines.sujato: grasping is a requirement for continued existence …
craving is a requirement for grasping …
feeling is a requirement for craving …
contact is a requirement for feeling …
the six sense fields are requirements for contact …
name and form are requirements for the six sense fields …
consciousness is a requirement for name and form …
choices are a requirement for consciousness …

above.sujato: (Saviṭṭha repeats exactly the same series of questions, and Nārada answers just as Musīla did.)
above.english: Here the Venerable Saviṭṭha asks the Venerable Narada the same series of questions as were addressed to the Venerable Musīla, and he answers in exactly the same way.

lines.pali: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:

below.pali: “Tenahāyasmā nārado arahaṁ khīṇāsavo”ti?
below.sujato: “Then Venerable Nārada is a perfected one, with defilements ended.”
below.english: “Then the Venerable Narada is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed.”

above.pali: Assosi kho āyasmā susimo:
above.sujato: Venerable Susīma heard about this.
above.english: The Venerable Susīma heard about this,

‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā”ti.

below.sujato: He went up to those mendicants, and exchanged greetings with them.

when name and form cease, the six sense fields cease …
when consciousness ceases name and form cease …

above.pali: “Kiṁ pana tvaṁ, kassapa, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno dīgharattaṁ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva …pe…

below.english: and spoken in praise of arousing energy?”

above.english: “Considering two benefits, venerable sir.

below.pali: Attano ca diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṁ sampassamāno, pacchimañca janataṁ anukampamāno:
below.sujato: I see happiness for myself in this life. And I have sympathy for future generations, thinking:
below.english: For myself I see a pleasant dwelling in this very life, and I have compassion for later generations, thinking,

above.pali: Ye kira te ahesuṁ buddhānubuddhasāvakā te dīgharattaṁ āraññikā ceva ahesuṁ āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino …pe…
above.sujato: For they may think: ‘It seems that the disciples awakened after the Buddha for a long time lived in the wilderness, ate only almsfood, wore rag robes, and owned just three robes; and they praised these things. They were of few wishes, content, secluded, aloof, and energetic; and they praised these things.’
above.english: For when they hear, ‘The enlightened disciples of the Buddha were for a long time forest dwellers and spoke in praise of forest dwelling …

below.pali: āraddhavīriyā ceva ahesuṁ vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādino’ti.

above.sujato: Seeing these two benefits I have long practiced these things.”

below.pali: āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.

above.english: so too, venerable sir, for one who has no faith in wholesome states, no sense of shame, no fear of wrongdoing, no energy, and no wisdom, whether day or night comes only decline is to be expected in regard to wholesome states, not growth.

below.sujato: A faithless individual is in decline.

below.sujato: A faithful individual doesn’t decline.
below.english: “A person with faith, venerable sir: this is a case of nondecline.

above.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, kassapa.

above.english: “Good, good, Kassapa!”

below.sujato: When there are mendicant advisers there is no decline.”
below.english: The Buddha then repeats the entire statement of the Venerable Mahakassapa.

above.pali: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti—
above.sujato: And so does Kassapa.
above.english: Kassapa too, to whatever extent he wishes, understands the minds of other beings and persons, having encompassed them with his own mind.

lines.pali: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāti …pe…
avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāti.

below.pali: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarāmi, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṁsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi, anekepi saṁvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṁvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe: ‘amutrāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhappaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṁ; tatrāpāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhappaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarāmi.
below.sujato: Whenever I want, I recollect my many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. I remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so I recollect my many kinds of past lives, with features and details.
below.english: “Bhikkhus, to whatever extent I wish, I recollect my manifold past abodes, that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of world-contraction and expansion thus: ‘There I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life span; passing away from there, I was reborn elsewhere, and there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life span; passing away from there, I was reborn here.’ Thus I recollect my manifold past abodes with their modes and details.

above.pali: “Tathā hi pana tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, imehi navehi bhikkhūhi indriyesu aguttadvārehi bhojane amattaññūhi jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttehi saddhiṁ cārikaṁ carasi, sassaghātaṁ maññe carasi, kulūpaghātaṁ maññe carasi.

above.english: “Friend Ānanda, it is just because you wander around with these young bhikkhus who are unguarded in their sense faculties….

below.pali: Na vāyaṁ kumārako mattamaññāsī”ti.

above.pali: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁ. Ekamantaṁ nisinno khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ etadavocaṁ:
above.sujato: So Nakula’s father told Sāriputta all that had happened, and said,
above.english: “Here, venerable sir, I approached the Blessed One…. The householder Nakulapita repeats his entire conversation with the Buddha.

lines.pali: ‘ahamasmi, bhante, jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto āturakāyo abhikkhaṇātaṅko.
Aniccadassāvī kho panāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato manobhāvanīyānañca bhikkhūnaṁ.
Evaṁ vutte, maṁ, bhante, bhagavā etadavoca:
Āturo hāyaṁ, gahapati, kāyo aṇḍabhūto pariyonaddho.

lines.sujato: When the mind is polluted, there’s no joy.
When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.
When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.
When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.
When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.

below.pali: Dhammānaṁ apātubhāvā pamādavihārītveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
below.sujato: Because principles have not become clear, you’re reckoned to live negligently.

above.english: If one dwells with restraint over the mind faculty, the mind is not soiled among mental phenomena cognizable by the mind….

lines.sujato: When the mind isn’t polluted, joy springs up.
When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.
When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss.
And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is immersed in samādhi, principles become clear.

lines.sujato: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
This is the disappearance of the world. …

above.english: mental phenomena cognizable by the mind.

lines.sujato: Because they still have greed, hate, and delusion, and have not given them up.

lines.sujato: Because they still have greed, hate, and delusion, and have not given them up.

below.pali: Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu yo rāgo so natthi, yo doso so natthi, yo moho so natthi, yo rāgo so pahīno, yo doso so pahīno, yo moho so pahīno, tassa adhimattā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti; ko pana vādo parittānaṁ.
below.sujato: Take any monk or nun who, when it comes to sights known by the eye, has no greed, hate, and delusion left, and has given them up. If even compelling sights come into their range of vision they don’t overcome their mind, let alone those that are trivial.
below.english: “Bhikkhus, in regard to forms cognizable by the eye, if in any bhikkhu or bhikkhunī lust does not exist and has been abandoned, if hatred does not exist and has been abandoned, if delusion does not exist and has been abandoned, then even prominent forms that enter into range of the eye do not obsess the mind, not to speak of those that are trifling.

above.pali: Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu …pe… manoviññeyyesu dhammesu yo rāgo so natthi, yo doso so natthi, yo moho so natthi, yo rāgo so pahīno, yo doso so pahīno, yo moho so pahīno, tassa adhimattā cepi manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti; ko pana vādo parittānaṁ.
above.sujato: When it comes to sounds … smells … tastes … touches … ideas known by the mind, they have no greed, hate, and delusion left, and have given them up. If even compelling ideas come into the range of the mind they don’t overcome their mind, let alone those that are trivial.
above.english: The same in regard to sounds cognizable by the ear … mental phenomena cognizable by the mind.

above.english: “So too, friend, the eye is not the fetter of forms …

for his mind is well freed.

“Imināpi kho etaṁ, āvuso, pariyāyena bhagavatā akkhātaṁ vivaṭaṁ pakāsitaṁ: ‘itipidaṁ viññāṇaṁ anattā’”ti …pe….

below.sujato: mind consciousness arise dependent on the mind and ideas?”
below.english: Doesn’t mind-consciousness arise in dependence on the mind and mental phenomena?”

above.pali: “Hatthesu, bhikkhave, sati ādānanikkhepanaṁ hoti;
above.sujato: “Mendicants, when there are hands, there’s picking up and putting down.
above.english: “Bhikkhus, when there are hands, there is picking up and putting down….

lines.sujato: When there are feet, there’s coming and going.
When there are joints, there’s contracting and extending.
When there’s a belly, there’s hunger and thirst.

below.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusmiṁ sati cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhaṁ dukkhaṁ …pe…

below.english: “So too, bhikkhus, when there is the eye, pleasure and pain arise internally with eye-contact as condition….

above.pali: Hatthesu, bhikkhave, asati ādānanikkhepanaṁ na hoti;
above.sujato: When there are no hands, there’s no picking up and putting down.
above.english: “When, bhikkhus, there are no hands, there is no picking up and putting down….

lines.sujato: When there are no feet, there’s no coming and going.
When there are no joints, there’s no contracting and extending.

lines.pali: kucchismiṁ asati jighacchā pipāsā na hoti.
lines.sujato: When there’s no belly, there’s no hunger and thirst.

below.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusmiṁ asati cakkhusamphassapaccayā nuppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhaṁ dukkhaṁ …pe…
below.sujato: In the same way, when there’s no eye, pleasure and pain don’t arise internally conditioned by eye contact.
below.english: “So too, bhikkhus, when there is no eye …

above.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, tañce bhikkhuṁ evaṁ carantaṁ evaṁ viharantaṁ rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā bhogehi abhihaṭṭhuṁ pavāreyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “In the same way, while that mendicant conducts themselves in this way and lives in this way, it may be that rulers or their chief ministers, friends or colleagues, relatives or family should invite them to accept wealth, saying,
above.english: “So too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is conducting himself thus and dwelling thus, kings or royal ministers, friends or colleagues, relatives or kinsmen, might invite him to accept wealth …

lines.pali: ‘ehi, bho purisa, kiṁ te ime kāsāvā anudahanti,
lines.sujato: ‘Please, my man, why let these ocher robes torment you?
Why follow the practice of shaving your head and carrying an alms bowl?

lines.pali: ehi hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjassu, puññāni ca karohī’ti.
lines.sujato: Come, return to a lesser life, enjoy wealth, and make merit!’

below.pali: So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ caranto evaṁ viharanto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
below.sujato: But it is quite impossible for a mendicant who conducts themselves in this way and lives in this way to resign the training and return to a lesser life.

above.english: an involvement with volitional formations …

Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti, saṅkhāragatametaṁ.

below.sujato: consciousness.
below.english: an involvement with consciousness.

above.pali: viññāṇaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, viññāṇasamudayaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, viññāṇanirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
above.sujato: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation, one thinks ‘a realized one still exists after death’ or
above.english: who does not know and see consciousness as it really is, who does not know and see its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation, that thinks: ‘The Tathagata exists after death’ … … or

lines.sujato: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ or

lines.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
lines.sujato: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ or

below.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”tipissa hoti.
below.sujato: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’
below.english: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’

above.pali: viññāṇaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, viññāṇasamudayaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, viññāṇanirodhaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ jānato passato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti;
above.sujato: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation, one doesn’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ or
above.english: consciousness as it really is, who knows and sees its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation, does not think: ‘The Tathagata exists after death’ … or

lines.pali: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti;
lines.sujato: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ or

lines.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti;
lines.sujato: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ or

below.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti.
below.sujato: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’
below.english: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’

above.pali: “Rūpārāmassa kho, āvuso, rūparatassa rūpasammuditassa rūpanirodhaṁ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṁ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
above.sujato: “Reverend, if you like, love, and enjoy form, and don’t truly see the cessation of form, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ or
above.english: i. Delight in the aggregates “Friend, it is one who delights in form, who takes delight in form, who rejoices in form, and who does not know and see the cessation of form as it really is, that thinks: ‘The Tathagata exists after death’ … or

lines.sujato: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ or

lines.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti;
lines.sujato: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ or

below.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipissa hoti.
below.sujato: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’
below.english: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’

above.pali: Tasmā tathāgatassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti—
above.sujato: That’s why, when asked, he does not declare one of those answers to be true.”
above.english: Therefore, when the Tathagata is asked such questions, he does not give such answers.”

lines.pali: neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇātipī”ti.

below.pali: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
below.sujato: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.
below.english: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and approached the Blessed One. He exchanged greetings with the Blessed One …and said to him:

above.pali: Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo, yena bhoto gotamassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
above.english: And what is the cause and reason why, when the ascetic Gotama is asked such questions, he does not give such answers?”

lines.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipī”ti?

below.pali: “Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā cakkhuṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti …pe…
below.english: “Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard the eye …

above.pali: Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yena bhoto gotamassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
above.sujato: And what’s the reason why, when the worthy Gotama is asked these questions, he does not declare one of these to be true?”
above.english: And what is the cause and reason why, when Master Gotama is asked such questions, he does not give such answers?”

lines.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipī”ti?

below.pali: “Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā rūpaṁ attato samanupassanti, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
below.sujato: “Vaccha, the wanderers of other religions regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
below.english: “Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form.

above.pali: Tathāgato ca kho, vaccha, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
above.sujato: The Realized One doesn’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
above.english: But, Vaccha, the Tathagata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not regard form as self …

below.pali: na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, na attani vā viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
below.sujato: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.
below.english: or self as in consciousness.

above.pali: Tasmā tathāgatassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
above.sujato: That’s why, when asked, he does not declare one of those answers to be true.”
above.english: Therefore, when the Tathagata is asked such questions, he does not give such answers.”

lines.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipī”ti.

below.pali: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
below.sujato: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and went to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, and exchanged greetings with him.
below.english: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and approached the Venerable Mahamoggallana. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Mahamoggallana …

above.pali: Ko pana, bho moggallāna, hetu, ko paccayo yena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṁ puṭṭhassa na evaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ hoti:
above.english: And what is the cause and reason why when the ascetic Gotama is asked such questions, he does not give such answers?”

lines.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipī”ti?

below.pali: “Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā rūpaṁ attato samanupassanti, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
below.english: “Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self …

above.pali: “Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā rūpaṁ attato samanupassanti, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
above.english: “Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self …

below.pali: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassanti, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
below.english: or self as in consciousness.

above.pali: Tathāgato ca kho, vaccha, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
above.english: But, Vaccha, the Tathagata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not regard form as self …

below.pali: na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, na attani vā viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
below.english: or self as in consciousness.

above.pali: ayampi kho ajito kesakambalo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa.
above.sujato: Ajita of the hair blanket leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.
above.english: This Ajita Kesakambalī …

lines.pali: Sopi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
lines.sujato: When a disciple passes away, he declares that
this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

below.pali: Yopissa sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tampi sāvakaṁ abbhatītaṁ kālaṅkataṁ upapattīsu byākaroti:
below.sujato: And as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he also declares that
below.english: when that disciple has passed away and died he also declares his rebirth thus:

above.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā vūpakaṭṭho viharanto taṁ dhammaṁ anussarati anuvitakketi, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti;
above.sujato: At such a time, a mendicant has initiated the awakening factor of mindfulness;
above.english: Whenever, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwelling thus withdrawn recollects that Dhamma and thinks it over, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is aroused by the bhikkhu; on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; on that occasion the enlightenment factor of mindfulness comes to fulfilment by development in the bhikkhu.

lines.pali: satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.

below.pali: So tathā sato viharanto taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṁsamāpajjati.
below.sujato: As they live mindfully in this way they investigate, explore, and inquire into that teaching with wisdom.
below.english: “Dwelling thus mindfully, he discriminates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, makes an investigation of it.

above.pali: Yasmiṁ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā sato viharanto taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṁsamāpajjati, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti;
above.sujato: At such a time, a mendicant has initiated the awakening factor of investigation of principles;
above.english: Whenever, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwelling thus mindfully discriminates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, makes an investigation of it, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of discrimination of states is aroused by the bhikkhu; on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of discrimination of states; on that occasion the enlightenment factor of discrimination of states comes to fulfilment by development in the bhikkhu.

lines.pali: dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṁ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchati.

below.pali: Tassa taṁ dhammaṁ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṁsamāpajjato āraddhaṁ hoti vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ.
below.sujato: As they investigate principles with wisdom in this way their energy is roused up and unflagging.
below.english: “While he discriminates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, makes an investigation of it, his energy is aroused without slackening.

above.pali: Satisambojjhaṅgo iti ce me, āvuso, hoti, ‘appamāṇo’ti me hoti, ‘susamāraddho’ti me hoti, tiṭṭhantañca naṁ ‘tiṭṭhatī’ti pajānāmi.
above.sujato: If it’s the awakening factor of mindfulness, I know that it’s limitless and that it’s properly implemented. While it remains I understand that it remains.
above.english: “If, friends, it occurs to me, ‘Let it be the enlightenment factor of mindfulness’ … all as above …

lines.pali: Sacepi me cavati, ‘idappaccayā me cavatī’ti pajānāmi …pe…
lines.sujato: And if it subsides I understand the specific reason it subsides. …

lines.pali: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo iti ce me, āvuso, hoti, ‘appamāṇo’ti me hoti, ‘susamāraddho’ti me hoti, tiṭṭhantañca naṁ ‘tiṭṭhatī’ti pajānāmi.
lines.sujato: If it’s the awakening factor of equanimity, I know that it’s limitless and that it’s properly implemented. While it remains I understand that it remains.

below.pali: Sacepi me cavati, ‘idappaccayā me cavatī’ti pajānāmī”ti.
below.sujato: And if it subsides I understand the specific reason it subsides.”
below.english: I understand, ‘It has abated in me for a particular reason.’”

above.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti?
above.sujato: And how does a mendicant with rational application of mind develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors?
above.english: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu who is accomplished in careful attention develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment?…” All as above.

lines.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ …pe…
lines.sujato: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

lines.pali: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.
lines.sujato: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

lines.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti.
lines.sujato: That’s how a mendicant with rational application of mind develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors.”

above.pali: Katamesaṁ sattannaṁ?
above.sujato: What seven?
above.english: What seven?” As above.

lines.sujato: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

lines.pali: imesaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ‘paññavā aneḷamūgo’ti vuccatī”ti.
lines.sujato: They’re called wise and clever because they’ve developed and cultivated these seven awakening factors.”

above.pali: Katamesaṁ sattannaṁ?
above.sujato: What seven?
above.english: What seven?” As above.

lines.sujato: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

lines.pali: imesaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā ‘daliddo’ti vuccatī”ti.
lines.sujato: They’re called poor because they haven’t developed and cultivated these seven awakening factors.”

above.pali: Katamesaṁ sattannaṁ?
above.sujato: What seven?
above.english: What seven?” As above.

lines.sujato: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

lines.pali: imesaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ‘adaliddo’ti vuccatī”ti.
lines.sujato: They’re called prosperous because they’ve developed and cultivated these seven awakening factors.”

above.pali: So sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
above.sujato: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.
above.english: If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ he dwells perceiving the repulsive therein….

lines.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati ‘paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
lines.sujato: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

lines.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
lines.sujato: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

lines.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
lines.sujato: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

below.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūlañca paṭikūlañca tadubhayaṁ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṁ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno.
below.sujato: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.
below.english: If he wishes: ‘Avoiding both the unrepulsive and the repulsive, may I dwell equanimously, mindful and clearly comprehending,’ then he dwells therein equanimously, mindful and clearly comprehending.

above.pali: Katame pañca?
above.sujato: What five?
above.english: as above …

lines.pali: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā,
lines.sujato: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

lines.pali: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
lines.sujato: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

below.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo.
below.sujato: This is not a mendicant’s own territory but the domain of others.
below.english: This is what is not a bhikkhu’s own resort but the domain of others.

above.pali: “diṭṭho me, bhante, bhagavato phāsu;
above.sujato: “Sir, it’s fantastic that the Buddha is comfortable,
above.english: “It’s splendid, venerable sir, that the Blessed One is bearing up, splendid that he has recovered!

below.pali: Api ca me, bhante, madhurakajāto viya kāyo, disāpi me na pakkhāyanti, dhammāpi maṁ nappaṭibhanti bhagavato gelaññena.
below.sujato: Because when the Buddha was sick, my body felt like it was drugged. I was disorientated, and the teachings didn’t spring to mind.
below.english: But, venerable sir, when the Blessed One was ill my body seemed as if it were drugged, I had become disoriented, the teachings were not clear to me.

above.pali: Tassa kismiñcideva pasādanīye nimitte cittaṁ paṇidahato pāmojjaṁ jāyati.
above.sujato: As they do so, joy springs up.
above.english: When he directs his mind towards some inspiring sign …

lines.sujato: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.
When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss.
And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

lines.pali: ‘yassa khvāhaṁ atthāya cittaṁ paṇidahiṁ, so me attho abhinipphanno.
lines.sujato: ‘I have accomplished the goal for which I directed my mind.

lines.pali: So paṭisaṁharati ceva na ca vitakketi na ca vicāreti.
lines.sujato: They relax, and neither place the mind nor keep it connected.

below.pali: ‘Avitakkomhi avicāro, ajjhattaṁ satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti.
below.sujato: They understand: ‘I’m neither placing the mind nor keeping it connected. Mindful within myself, I’m happy.’
below.english: He understands: ‘Without thought and examination, internally mindful, I am happy.’

above.pali: “Na ca kho me, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto sīlakkhandhaṁ vā ādāya parinibbuto, samādhikkhandhaṁ vā …pe…
above.sujato: “No, sir, he did not.
above.english: “No, he did not, venerable sir.

below.pali: Api ca me, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto ovādako ahosi otiṇṇo viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako, akilāsu dhammadesanāya, anuggāhako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
below.sujato: But Venerable Sāriputta was my adviser and counselor. He educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired me. He never tired of teaching the Dhamma, and he supported his spiritual companions.
below.english: But for me the Venerable Sāriputta was an advisor and counsellor, one who instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened me. He was unwearying in teaching the Dhamma; he was helpful to his brothers in the holy life.

above.pali: Katame cattāro?
above.sujato: What four?
above.english: all as above …

lines.pali: Kāye vā, bhante, bhikkhu kāyānupassī vihareyya ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
lines.sujato: A mendicant would meditate observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
Or they’d meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

lines.pali: dhammesu vā, bhante, bhikkhu dhammānupassī vihareyya ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
lines.sujato: or principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

below.pali: Ekāyanvāyaṁ, bhante, maggo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ—cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti.
below.sujato: The four kinds of mindfulness meditation are the path to convergence. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.”

above.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so puriso sirivaḍḍhassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: “Yes, sir,” that man replied. He did as Sirivaḍḍha asked.
above.english: “Yes, master,” that man replied, and he approached the Venerable Ānanda, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and delivered his message.

lines.pali: “sirivaḍḍho, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno, so āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandati.
‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena sirivaḍḍhassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.

below.sujato: Ānanda consented with silence.

lines.sujato: The practice that leads to the cessation of suffering is the fourth noble truth I’ve taught, and that’s how you should remember it.

lines.pali: Yo hi koci, bhikkhu, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṁ vadeyya:
lines.sujato: For if any ascetic or brahmin should say this:

below.pali: ‘netaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā catutthaṁ ariyasaccaṁ yaṁ samaṇena gotamena desitaṁ.
below.sujato: ‘What the ascetic Gotama teaches is not the fourth noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.
below.english: ‘This is not the fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering taught by the ascetic Gotama;

above.pali: ‘vādamassa āropessāmī’ti, taṁ vata sahadhammena saṅkampessati vā sampakampessati vā sampacālessati vāti—netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
above.sujato: ‘I’ll refute their doctrine!’ It’s simply impossible for them to legitimately make that mendicant shake or rock or tremble.
above.english: ‘I will refute his thesis,’ it is impossible that he could make that bhikkhu shake, quake, or tremble.

below.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, silāyūpo soḷasa kukkuko.
below.sujato: Suppose there was a stone post, sixteen feet long.
below.english: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a stone column sixteen yards long:

above.pali: puratthimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā vādatthiko vādagavesī ‘vādamassa āropessāmī’ti, taṁ vata sahadhammena saṅkampessati vā sampakampessati vā sampacālessati vāti—netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
above.sujato: An ascetic or brahmin might come from the east, west, north, or south wanting to debate, seeking a debate, thinking: ‘I’ll refute their doctrine!’ It’s simply impossible for them to legitimately make that mendicant shake or rock or tremble.
above.english: and then an ascetic or a brahmin comes along … it is impossible that he could make that bhikkhu shake, quake, or tremble.

lines.pali: dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā vādatthiko vādagavesī: ‘vādamassa āropessāmī’ti, taṁ vata sahadhammena saṅkampessati vā sampakampessati vā sampacālessati vāti—netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.

above.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando vesāliṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then Ānanda wandered for alms in Vesālī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: Then, when the Venerable Ānanda had walked for alms in Vesali and had returned from his alms round, after his meal he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported what he had seen.

lines.pali: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁ.
